ISOMPRA enables the disambiguation of transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects of genetic variants
items.abstract: Abstract Some classic massively parallel reporter assays to study transcriptional regulatory effects of DNA sequence elements cannot readily distinguish these from post-transcriptional regulatory effects of the same element on RNA. Therefore, we developed an approach enabling assessment of DNA/RNA regulatory elements in parallel: Inferred Stability Optimized Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (ISOMPRA). ISOMPRA quantifies pre-spliced RNA to more directly assess transcription rate, and spliced RNA, corrected for transcription rate, to identify RNA stability-altering 3′-UTR elements. We benchmark ISOMPRA with both predicted enhancers and 3′-UTR elements, including regions containing autism patient mutations. We identify numerous functional enhancers and UTRs and discover a subset with high-impact mutations. We further show that failing to consider both potential transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects results in numerous possible false positives and false negatives. Finally, we adapt ISOMPRA for cell-type-specific in vivo use, enabling analyses of variants in specific cell types in the brain and measurement of regulatory impacts of in vivo traits, such as sex.

items.title: Modular mRNA-encoded helper proteins enhance DNA delivery
items.abstract: Abstract DNA delivery is limited by inefficient nuclear translocation and restrictive intracellular environments. Here we present mRNA-enhanced DNA delivery (MEND), a system that codelivers mRNA-encoded helper proteins to actively prime cells for enhanced DNA processing. We demonstrate three classes of MEND proteins: DNA translocators, host modulators and immune dampeners. MEND’s modular framework boosts transgene expression across various delivery vehicles and DNA formats in vitro and in vivo with LNP delivery.

items.title: Exhaustive rearrangement of an enhancer reveals that dependency-syntax encodes tissue specificity
items.abstract: Abstract Enhancers direct precise gene expression patterns, but how syntax, the organization of transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs), shapes enhancer activity and tissue specificity remains unclear. Here we test 460,800 organizations of ETS and GATA TFBSs in Ciona embryos. All elements contain the same number, type and affinity of TFBSs, yet only 18% are active. Single TFBS orientation flips convert 54,000 inert elements into functional enhancers, establishing syntax as a critical determinant of enhancer activity and revealing strict syntax rules. We identify enhancer syntaxes in which activity depends on placement of differing-affinity TFBSs (dependent-syntax) and robust-syntaxes that are active regardless of TFBS affinity placement. We develop a Single-cell, whole-Embryo Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (SEMPRA), which shows that dependent-syntax is critical for maintaining sensitivity to the trans environment and tissue specificity, whereas robust-syntaxes yield broadly active enhancers. Our exhaustive enhancer rearrangement coupled with whole-embryo MPRA and SEMPRA reveals that enhancer syntax tunes responsiveness to the cellular environment, thereby encoding tissue specificity.

items.title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
items.abstract: Abstract Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

items.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
items.abstract: Abstract Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target.

Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
items.abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Here, we show CD1a reactivity in subsets of human circulating and cutaneous CD4 + Treg cells, displaying αβ T cell receptors (TCRs), memory phenotypes and suppressive functions, including the ability to secrete interleukin-10 (IL-10) in response to the permissive lipid antigen lysophosphatidylcholine, known to be enriched in skin inflammation. Moreover, CD1a-reactive IL-10-producing CD4 + Treg cells from patients with psoriasis up-regulate type 1 and type 17 pro-inflammatory signatures under in vitro stimulation, while a corresponding Treg cell population is enriched and dysfunctional in psoriatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analyses suggest that CD1a-reactive Treg cell signatures are localized in close proximity to CD1a⁺ antigen-presenting cells within psoriatic lesions and are potentially connected through ligand-receptor interactions relevant to cell-cell contact, recruitment, and functional regulation. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

Rethinking Klebsiella pneumoniae vaccines: from protective immunity to rational vaccine design
items.abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae infections cause hundreds of thousands of deaths annually, yet a licensed vaccine remains elusive. Current strategies targeting capsular polysaccharides and lipopolysaccharides show promise but face limitations due to the complexity of Klebsiella pathogenesis and incomplete understanding of protective immunity. This Review highlights the critical barriers hindering broad protection against K. pneumoniae . We argue that next-generation vaccines require a paradigm shift, integrating antigen discovery, systems immunology and translational models to define conserved protective targets and immune correlates. This holistic strategy is essential to predict vaccine efficacy and finally combat this escalating global health threat.

items.title: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
items.abstract: Abstract A pause in DNA synthesis that occurs when the replisome encounters an obstacle could lead to genome instability. Although important, systematic identification of replication pause sites is challenging due to their low frequency and delocalised nature. Here we present a single-molecule identification of sites of replisome perturbation across a eukaryotic genome using long-read nanopore sequencing. For each single-molecule replication pause we determine the direction of replication, leading/lagging-strand identity, location and approximate duration, and whether the replisome resumed synthesis. Although pauses are largely diffuse over the genome, they are significantly enriched over transcribed features and correlate with transcription and R-loop levels. Transcription-replication conflicts are more numerous when head-on than co-directional. Finally, we identify genomic loci with a strong bias towards leading over lagging strand pauses, consistent with uncoupling of the helicase from polymerase epsilon. As one such locus overlaps with an epigenetically-regulated gene, we suggest that helicase-polymerase uncoupling resulting from replication pausing could trigger epigenetic switching.

Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
items.abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GID Gid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Taken together, our results establish Gid11 as a bona fide GID substrate receptor and highlight GID as a regulator of metabolic transitions.

Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
items.abstract: Abstract Toll-like receptors (TLRs) support T cell priming in lymphatic tissues, but whether TLR stimulation within tumors also affects T cell function locally remains undefined. Here, we show that TLR2 signaling is necessary to promote CD8 + T cell-mediated tumor control by dual intravenous and intratumoral delivery of attenuated Listeria monocytogenes (IV + IT Lm ). TLR2 signaling supports T cell priming in the spleen during IV infection, but unexpectedly, TLR2 is also critical for the activity of anti- Lm CD8 + T cells in tumors upon IT Lm injection. TLR2 signaling is unique among all TLRs in its capacity to drive a cDC2-dependent reduction in regulatory T cells (Treg) and destabilize Foxp3 expression. TLR2-mediated Treg destabilization correlates with increased tumor antigen cross-presentation and stronger antitumor CD8 + T cell responses. Ultimately, TLR2-dependent Treg depletion is required for tumor control by IV + IT Lm . These findings reveal a novel role for TLR2 activation by bacteria in tumors to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance tumor-specific T cell responses.

Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
items.abstract: Abstract Aneuploidy, resulting from whole-chromosome or segmental gains and losses, is generally detrimental to organismal fitness and is strongly associated with tumorigenesis. While sex chromosome aneuploidies are relatively well tolerated due to dedicated allelic dosage compensation mechanisms, the existence of comparable regulatory processes for autosomes remains debated. Here, we investigate transcriptional responses to autosomal aneuploidy and identify widespread dosage compensation across affected chromosomes. Using high-sensitivity allele-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing of monoclonal cell expansions spanning diverse ploidies and degrees of aneuploidy, we uncover consistent transcriptional compensation of both chromosomal gains and losses. This response operates in a region-specific manner across both complete and segmental aneuploidies, revealing an unexpected flexibility in dosage regulation. We show that chromosome losses are compensated through increased transcriptional burst frequency from the remaining allele. Complementary proteomics analyses demonstrate additional buffering at the protein level, resulting in a substantial, though still incomplete, restoration of stoichiometric balance across autosomal aneuploid chromosomes for both copy number gains and losses. Analyses of cancer transcriptomes confirm that compensatory mechanisms are active in human tumours. Together, our findings establish dosage compensation as a genome-wide and dynamic response to gene dose imbalance. This mechanism extends beyond sex chromosomes, supports transcriptional homeostasis, and represents a fundamental and evolutionarily conserved mode of gene regulation active across species and in aneuploid cancer cells.

items.title: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
items.abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus is a human bacterial pathogen with an array of molecular mechanisms to evade the action of antibiotics. Within the organism, efflux pumps provide a first-line defense mechanism, enabling broad multidrug resistance across antibiotic classes and the ability for the organism to evolve target-level resistance mechanisms. NorA is a key efflux transporter in S. aureus responsible for conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, puromycin, and other cytotoxic compounds. Here, we describe an approach to develop peptide efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) of NorA by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement and S. aureus growth inhibition. Our cryo-EM structure reveals that a lead peptide NPI-5 inserts deeply into NorA’s substrate binding pocket by using two tryptophan-arginine motifs to bind an anionic patch within NorA, thereby stabilizing the outward-facing conformation of the transporter and halting antibiotic efflux. Further optimization of NPI-5 involving unnatural residues and macrocyclization yielded cNPI-7, a peptide which potentiates fluoroquinolones in vitro and in a murine bacteremia infection model. The successful development of potent and selective peptide-based EPIs provides an approach for inhibiting other efflux systems from pathogenic organisms.

items.title: CD33-CD45 interaction in Alzheimer’s disease susceptibility
A meta-analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation in endometriosis
items.abstract: Abstract Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting 10% of women, characterized by the growth of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus. Through a genome-wide DNA methylation meta-analysis of nine independent cohorts ( n = 1138 samples), we show an epigenetic dichotomy: the eutopic endometrium of endometriosis cases shows no significant divergence from healthy controls, whereas ectopic lesions exhibit massive, consistent hyper/hypomethylation. We identify 1824 differentially methylated regions targeting the HOX clusters, ESR1 , and GATA2 , key regulators of cell differentiation and hormonal response. This suggests that endometriotic cells possess an epigenetic identity distinct from normal endometrial cells. While most alterations reflect biological mechanisms shared across anatomical sites, distinct signatures exist between lesion types. By harmonizing independent datasets, our study provides a high-resolution molecular map of lesions and strengthens the evidence that DNA methylation drives endometriosis biology.

items.title: 3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
items.abstract: Abstract Investigating the movements and conformational changes of proteins in living cells is essential for understanding their function. The recently introduced fluorescence nanoscopy method called MINSTED has successfully tracked single fluorophore-labelled proteins, albeit in fixed cells and two dimensions only. Here we introduce a MINSTED setup for live-cell tracking of individual proteins in three dimensions (3D) with a localization precision σ down to <1 nm. Applied to the motor protein kinesin-1, our MINSTED nanoscope follows single proteins in 3D as they process along microtubules in 16 nm steps. Individual steps are resolved amid substantial intracellular background. The unique capability of the 3D stimulated emission depletion (STED) beam to carve out the signal of the protein label of interest enables efficient single-molecule investigations at hitherto unpractically high concentrations of labelled proteins and thus in crowded live-cell environments.

Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
items.abstract: Abstract Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a −1 to ~1000 m a −1 before dropping to ~50 m a −1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s −1 ), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

A long-read metagenomic catalog of near-finished bacterial genomes from Shanghai pet dogs captures gut microbial diversity across geographically distinct cohorts
items.abstract: Abstract Background Pet dogs are considered part of the family, and understanding their gut microbiomes can provide insights into both animal and household health. Most comprehensive studies, however, relied on short-read sequencing, resulting in fragmented metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) that miss mobile genetic elements, antimicrobial resistance genes, and ribosomal genes. Results We apply deep long-read metagenomics, polished with short reads, to fecal samples from 51 urban pet dogs in Shanghai, generating 2,676 MAGs representing 320 bacterial species. Approximately 72% of these MAGs achieve near-finished quality and often improve on the corresponding publicly available reference genomes. Comparisons with external datasets show that our Shanghai-based MAG catalog is representative of urban pet dogs worldwide, with a median read-mapping rate above 90%. Moreover, we retrieve 185 nonredundant clusters of circular extrachromosomal elements, including elements linked to antimicrobial resistance, which are also detected in external dog gut datasets. Finally, long-read metagenomics reveals a dynamic genome architecture, including a putative secondary chromosome in a Fusobacterium species. Conclusions We provide a high-quality reference resource and demonstrate the power of deep long-read metagenomics to resolve microbial diversity and genome architecture in complex host-associated microbiomes.

Donor-specific assemblies enhance somatic structural variant detection in complex genomic regions
items.last_author_affiliation: University of Washington, Brotman Baty Institute for Precision Medicine
items.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) contribute substantially to genomic variation and disease, but detecting somatic SVs (sSVs) remains difficult due to reference bias, mosaicism, and enrichment in repetitive regions. Linear reference genomes, like GRCh38 and CHM13, do not fully capture individual genomic structure, which can obscure true somatic variation. Donor-specific assemblies (DSAs) generated from the same genome where sSVs are being assayed provide a personalized alternative, yet their performance for sSV detection has not been systematically assessed. As part of the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network, we benchmark a DSA for sSV discovery in the COLO829 melanoma cell line with a matched normal sample from the same individual. We compare sSV detection across GRCh38, CHM13, and COLO829BL_DSA using three sSV callers (DELLY, Severus, and Sniffles2) and multiple long-read sequencing platforms and validate candidate calls through visual inspection of aligned reads. COLO829BL_DSA identifies 1.8-fold more validated sSVs than linear references, in regions both shared with GRCh38 and CHM13 and unique to COLO829BL_DSA. Variants detected only with COLO829BL_DSA are often found in satellite and other repeat-rich regions that are difficult to resolve using standard references, including two variants in cancer-associated genes not identified by either linear reference. We further identify caller-, platform-, and region-specific filtering strategies that substantially improve precision, offering a more scalable path toward high-confidence sSV detection. Overall, these results underscore the utility of DSAs, alongside practical strategies for their analysis, in improving sSV detection.

items.title: Somatic haplotyping for tumor DNA fraction estimation and variant recalibration with LongPhase-S
items.last_author_affiliation: National Chung Cheng University;
items.abstract: Accurate detection of somatic variants is crucial for precision oncology, and long-read sequencing offers unprecedented advantages in resolving complex cancer genomes. However, most long-read somatic callers rely on phasing built for a diploid genome, an assumption that tumor contamination, subclonal heterogeneity, and aneuploidy violate. We present LongPhase-S, a novel method that jointly reconstructs somatic haplotypes, infers tumor DNA fraction, and recalibrates somatic variants in a fraction-aware manner for paired tumor-normal long-read sequencing. By anchoring each somatic read to a parental germline lineage, LongPhase-S provides a phase-resolved view in which germline and somatic reads are disentangled across the genome. Building on somatic haplotyping, LongPhase-S estimates tumor DNA fraction with performance matching or exceeding existing unphased methods, providing the basis for fraction-aware variant recalibration. Using eight ONT benchmark datasets comprising six cancer cell lines, including breast, melanoma, and lung cancers, LongPhase-S improves the accuracy of state-of-the-art somatic callers. Specifically, mean F1 scores increase by 4.5% and 7.1% for single-nucleotide variants and indels with ClairS, and by 1.2% and 0.5% with DeepSomatic. In six additional PacBio HiFi dilution-series datasets, the same ONT-trained model and variant recalibration generalized without retraining. Collectively, these results show that somatic haplotyping is a critical yet missing piece in existing somatic callers and enables fraction-aware and phase-resolved variant interpretation in heterogeneous tumors.

items.title: The RNAdecayCafe atlas of RNA half-life estimates across multiple human cell lines
items.last_author_affiliation: Yale University
items.abstract: RNA expression levels are partially determined by RNA stabilities. Long-lived RNAs accumulate to higher levels than rapidly degraded RNAs when transcribed at the same rate. The extent to which RNA decay contributes to differences in gene expression between genes in the same cell or between different cell types has not been extensively examined. This is in part because reproducible RNA half-life estimates from different biological contexts have not been broadly collected and curated. To address this, we have developed RNAdecayCafe, a database of high-quality RNA half-life estimates in multiple human cell lines. RNAdecayCafe makes use of pulse-label nucleotide recoding RNA-seq data (namely SLAM-seq and TimeLapse-seq), which we found to provide consistent and orthogonally validated half-life estimates. In total, RNAdecayCafe provides half-life estimates from 11 different human cell lines across 15 datasets and a total of 64 samples that were uniformly processed with a set of optimized bioinformatic tools we recently developed (the EZbakR suite). We showcase how this resource affirms and enables deeper investigations of the role RNA stability regulation plays in shaping gene expression. RNAdecayCafe will provide a robust database for future studies of RNA decay. We have distributed the database as a Zenodo repository and the data can be browsed via a web application.

items.title: Exploring and visualizing complex pangenome graphs with PanAbyss
items.last_author_affiliation: Universite de Toulouse, INRAE, MIAT
items.abstract: The pangenome paradigm enables a more comprehensive capture of structural variants than traditional linear-reference-based approaches. Recent advances in graph-based pangenome construction and increasing availability of high-quality telomere-to-telomere assemblies now make it possible to represent genomic diversity more effectively, including structural rearrangements and intergenic regions that were previously underexplored. However, few tools allow researchers to interactively explore the complex landscape of a pangenome, particularly for large variation graphs. Here, we present PanAbyss, an application built around a novel data model that enables both the visualization of annotated graph segments and the identification and characterization of regions of interest. This approach allows PanAbyss to offer unique functionalities, including the ability to query a region by annotation, to search for regions shared among specific individuals in the graph, compute proximity trees between individuals, and retrieve sequences associated with targeted regions. PanAbyss thus provides a versatile and user-friendly platform for in-depth pangenome exploration. To illustrate its utility, we present a use case focusing on the identification of structural variants associated with the white head phenotype in cattle, and compare our findings to previously reported results.

items.title: MaxGeomHash bridges MinHash and FracMinHash for scalable similarity estimation using sub-linear k -mer sketching
items.last_author_affiliation: Universitat Politecnica de Catalunya
items.abstract: With the surge in sequencing data generated from biological studies, designing scalable computational techniques has become essential. One effective strategy to enable large-scale computation is to extract k -mers from long sequences, and summarize large k -mer sets into random samples (a.k.a. sketches). These sketches enable rapid estimation of similarity metrics such as Jaccard or cosine, and thus facilitate scalable computations. Popular sketching tools in bioinformatics range from the MinHash algorithm to generate fixed-size sketches; to FracMinHash algorithm to retain a fraction of all k -mers. Here, we introduce a novel sketching algorithm, MaxGeomHash, which for a specified integer parameter b ≥ 1, will produce a random sample of size b lg(n/b) + O(b) without knowing the total number of k -mers n beforehand. Notably, this is the first permutation-invariant and parallelizable sketching algorithm to date that can produce sublinear sketches. We also introduce a variant, α-MaxGeomHash, that produces sketches of size Θ(n α ) for a given α; ∈ (0, 1). We study the algorithm's properties, analyze generated sample sizes, verify theoretical results empirically, provide a fast implementation, and investigate similarity estimate quality. With intermediate-sized samples between constant (MinHash) and linear (FracMinHash), MaxGeomHash balances efficiency (smaller samples need less processing) with accuracy (larger samples yield better estimates). On genomic datasets, we demonstrate that MaxGeomHash enables pairwise similarity estimation at a large scale, and MaxGeomHash sketches enable similarity estimation more accurately than MinHash, and more efficiently than FracMinHash.

items.title: Engineering genome instability at repetitive elements reveals distinct roles for balanced rearrangements and ploidy in adaptation of a human fungal pathogen
items.last_author_affiliation: University of Kent;
items.abstract: Genome plasticity is a ubiquitous feature of eukaryotic life, yet how different forms of genome variation contribute to biological adaptation remains poorly understood. Fungal pathogens exploit genome instability for adapting rapidly to stress. In the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans , structural variation frequently arises at repetitive DNA elements and generates balanced chromosomal rearrangements, loss of heterozygosity and aneuploidy. Because these genome alterations often coexist in clinical isolates, their individual contributions to adaptation remain difficult to resolve. Here, we describe Repetitive Element-Directed Cas9 (RED-Cas9), a genome engineering approach that introduces targeted double-strand breaks at two major C. albicans repeat families. By generating multiple classes of structural variation within the same genetic background, RED-Cas9 enables the direct comparison of their biological consequences, avoiding the confounding effects of unrelated genetic variation present in clinical isolates. We show that balanced rearrangements, which rearrange chromosomes without altering gene dosage, produced minimal transcriptional changes and no large-effect phenotypes. In contrast, ploidy variation triggered widespread gene dosage-linked transcriptional reprogramming and distinct phenotypic outcomes, including fluconazole resistance, impaired filamentation, and reduced virulence. These findings establish RED-Cas9 as a platform to dissect the functional consequences of distinct classes of structural variation and demonstrate that balanced chromosomal rearrangements and chromosome copy-number changes make fundamentally different contributions to genome plasticity and adaptation in a human fungal pathogen.

items.title: Alu and core duplicon sequences drive 16p12.3-p13.11 segmental duplication expansion and structural diversity through multiple mechanisms
items.last_author_affiliation: University of Milan;
items.abstract: Human and ape genomes contain regions enriched in interspersed segmental duplications (SDs) that promote gene innovation and predispose to pathogenic rearrangements. Mechanisms driving SD expansion in the human genome remain poorly understood, although SDs cluster around high-copy ancestral core duplicons and exhibit Alu enrichment at their boundaries. Here, we investigate structural diversity and evolution at the disease-associated 16p12.3-p13.11 locus, comprising four SD clusters organized around the LCR16a core duplicon. Analysis of 94 haploid human genomes reveals 12 alternative structural configurations across clusters 1-2 and eight across clusters 3-4, with different predicted susceptibilities to pathogenic rearrangements. These include two deletions and four inversions arising through nonallelic homologous recombination (NAHR) or nonhomologous end joining. We identify two types of multiallelic tandem duplications involving LCR16a and an adjacent segment, both arising through Alu-Alu NAHR. We characterize two complex insertions whose structures and breakpoint features support models involving double template switching, preferentially involving homologous sites within LCR16a duplicons (empirical p = 3 x 10 -4 ) and/or Alu elements (empirical p = 0.029). Evolutionary analyses suggest that clusters 3 and 4 expanded approximately 6 million years ago in the human-chimpanzee common ancestor through double template switching involving Alu repeats. Clusters 1 and 2 expanded through two human-specific duplicative transpositions, possibly mediated by circular DNA intermediates, with LCR16a sequences at both reintegration breakpoints and insertion sites, generating the human-specific NOMO1 gene. These findings implicate Alu elements and LCR16a duplicons in SD formation and genomic instability at 16p12.3-p13.11 through recombination-, replication-, and circular DNA-based mechanisms.

items.title: Epigenetic and transcriptomic clocks capture independent aging signals and reveal nfixb as a modifier of epigenetic aging in a model teleost
items.last_author_affiliation: University of Georgia
items.abstract: Biological aging progresses at different rates across individuals, yet identifying the molecular determinants underlying this variation remains a central challenge. Using whole-genome bisulfite sequencing and transcriptomic profiling of hepatic tissue from the model fish species, Japanese medaka ( Oryzias latipes ), we develop and compare epigenetic and transcriptomic aging clocks to assess how distinct molecular modalities capture aging signals across the lifespan. Both clocks accurately predict chronological age, although CpG methylation-based models outperform those derived from gene expression. Critically, the relative age acceleration metrics from these two clocks are largely uncorrelated, indicating that they capture distinct facets of biological aging. Despite this lack of correlated aging signal, age-associated changes in DNA methylation and gene expressions display patterns of spatial overlap, suggesting localized regulatory interactions. Genetic association scans of sequenced exomes identify variants associated with age acceleration metrics. In particular, variants within a region containing nfixb and rad23a exert strong effects on epigenetic age estimates, a finding which is validated in an independent cohort. Age-associated methylation at nfixb transcription start sites, together with genotype-specific effects on methylation and exon usage, implicate nfixb as a modifier of epigenetic aging. Comparative methylome analyses reveal conserved age-related methylation at nfixb/Nfix in medaka and mice, and is consistent with recent findings implicating a role for NF1 transcription factors in human epigenetic aging. Collectively, these findings show epigenetic and transcriptomic clocks capture distinct aging dimensions shaped by genetic and stochastic factors. They highlight the modular architecture of aging and position medaka as a powerful model for dissecting conserved mechanisms of vertebrate aging.

items.title: ChromSkills enables interpretable and domain-guided agentic chromatin data analysis.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Cardiovascular Diseases and Medical Innovation Center, Institute for Regenerative Medicine, Department of Neurosurgery, Shanghai Key Laboratory of Signaling and Disease Research, Frontier Science Center for Stem Cell Research, School of Life Sciences and Technology, Shanghai East Hospital, Tongji University, Shanghai, 200092, China. yzhang@tongji.edu.cn.
items.abstract: High-throughput chromatin assays require flexible workflows and context-aware parameter choices. However, unconstrained large language model-based analysis can suffer from inconsistent tool selection, parameterization, and execution. We present ChromSkills, a curated library of domain-specific analytical Skills for agentic chromatin data analysis on coding-agent platforms that support Skills. ChromSkills encodes expert decision logic and parameter-selection rules as modular, human-readable Skills linked to structured tool interfaces, enabling interpretable workflow composition and consistent execution from natural-language tasks. Across representative analyses, ChromSkills improved tool and parameter consistency, execution stability, and token efficiency, providing a transparent and domain-guided framework for AI-assisted chromatin data analysis.

items.title: Single-molecule long-read sequencing reveals transcriptome complexity and enhances annotation in wild rice.
items.last_author_affiliation: ARC Centre for Plant Success in Nature and Agriculture, University of Queensland, Brisbane, QLD, 4067, Australia. robert.henry@uq.edu.au.; VinUni Big Data Research Institute, VinUniversity, Hanoi, Vietnam. robert.henry@uq.edu.au.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Wild rice species harbour extensive but largely uncharacterised transcriptional diversity that underpins key agronomic traits and represents a valuable resource for crop improvement. Here we integrate single-molecule long-read sequencing (Iso-Seq) with short-read RNA-seq to resolve transcriptomes of Australian Oryza rufipogon-like (O. rufipogon Aus) and O. meridionalis, the closest and most phylogenetically distant AA-genome relatives of Asian domesticated rice, respectively. RESULTS: Iso-Seq reveals substantially greater transcriptome complexity than represented in current reference annotations, identifying 48,876 transcript isoforms in O. rufipogon Aus and 69,180 in O. meridionalis. More than 60% of annotated genes are captured, and over 40% exhibit alternative isoforms, compared with approximately 10% in existing annotations. Integration of Iso-Seq data substantially improves genome annotations by restoring untranslated regions, increasing gene and transcript models, and improving BUSCO completeness. We identify 2,021 novel genes in O. rufipogon Aus and 2,645 in O. meridionalis, resolve hundreds of mis-assembled fusion genes, and uncover thousands of previously unannotated isoforms, including species-specific protein-coding transcripts and long non-coding RNAs. Analysis of three grain-size regulators (OsMADS1, GS1, and SGW5) reveals substantial isoform diversity in wild rice. Notably, functional OsMADS1 and GS1 isoforms previously identified in domesticated rice populations are also detected in wild species, demonstrating that multiple functional transcript variants exist prior to domestication. Iso-Seq further identifies O. rufipogon-specific splice variants and reduced SGW5 expression associated with its narrow-grain phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings uncover hidden transcriptional complexity in wild rice, substantially refine genome annotations, and provide valuable resources for functional transcript studies and precise isoform-level quantification.

items.title: Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ-1.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Life Science, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China. zhuyalan@bit.edu.cn.; Advanced Technology Research Institute, Beijing Institute of Technology, Jinan, China. zhuyalan@bit.edu.cn.
items.abstract: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune systems are powerful and versatile tools for genome engineering. CRISPR-Casδ-1 is a recently discovered, evolutionarily distinct endonuclease that enables versatile cross-kingdom genome editing under miniature RNA-guiding. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural characterization of CRISPR-Casδ-1. Biochemical analysis not only verifies that Casδ-1 exhibits robust double-stranded DNA cleavage activity and target-dependent trans-cleavage activity, but also explores in depth its precise cleavage sites and substrate saturation. Furthermore, we determine a 3.04 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of the Casδ-1-crRNA-dsDNA ternary complex, which reveals the molecular basis of protospacer-adjacent motif (PAM) recognition, crRNA-DNA heteroduplex assembly, and RuvC domain-mediated DNA cleavage. Collectively, our study reveals the structural basis and evolutionary insights into Casδ-1, advances the mechanistic understanding of type V CRISPR-Cas effectors, and offers opportunities for the rational design of CRISPR-Casδ-1 as a versatile genome-editing tool.

items.title: Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Environmental and Resource Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. kyang@zju.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Soil Pollution Control and Safety, Hangzhou, China. kyang@zju.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory of Environmental Pollution and Ecological Health of Ministry of Education, Hangzhou, China. kyang@zju.edu.cn.; Zhejiang University-Hangzhou Global Scientific and Technological Innovation Center, Hangzhou, China. kyang@zju.edu.cn.; Zhejiang Provincial Key Laboratory of Organic Pollution Process and Control, Hangzhou, China. kyang@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Minimizing H2O2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H2O2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H2O2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H2O2 (0.5 mM), with H2O2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination.

items.title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Biomedical Engineering, Tsinghua Medicine, Tsinghua University, Beijing, P.R. China. ningguochen@tsinghua.edu.cn.; School of Clinical Medicine (Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital), Tsinghua Medicine, Tsinghua University, Beijing, P.R. China. ningguochen@tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings.

items.title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Physics, East China Normal University, Shanghai, P. R. China. ljhuang@phy.ecnu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces.

items.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Neural Science, New York University, New York, NY, 10003, USA.
items.abstract: Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain's internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain's compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

items.title: From microstructure to function: spatial visualization of magnetic permeability.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Advanced Materials, Shanghai Key Lab of Molecular Catalysis and Innovative Materials, State Key Laboratory of Coatings for Advanced Equipment, Electron Microscopy Center, College of Smart Materials and Future Energy, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. rcche@fudan.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Understanding the physics of high-frequency magnetic response is essential for advancing electromagnetic materials. Here, a general strategy is presented for visualizing magnetic permeability as a spatially distributed, frequency-dependent field, instead of a uniform bulk parameter. Our framework reveals that high-frequency magnetic loss arises from coherent spin-wave propagation and interference, leading to spatially selective energy absorption and localized regions of negative imaginary permeability. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. Computational modeling provides an ideal platform to complement experimental exploration. The physic-data framework reveals geometry-to-spectra design rules, validated on iron nanoparticles. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing.

items.title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Marine Materials, Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Ningbo, China. liuxq@nimte.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

items.title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Integrated Circuits, Wuhan National High Magnetic Field Center, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. xfli@hust.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Wurtzite-structured aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric materials are potential candidates for non-volatile memory (NVM) applications because of their high remanent polarization (Pr > 100 μC·cm-2) and compatibility with back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes. However, achieving high-performance wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) remains a significant challenge because of their high interface trap density (Dit) and large threshold voltage (VTH) variation. Here we show the distinct polarization switching mechanisms of AlScN FeFETs based on an ultrathin indium gallium oxide (IGO) channel with three different structures. FeFETs with a metal-ferroelectric-metal-insulator-semiconductor (MFMIS) structure show high interface quality with low Dit and a stable VTH, achieving a large memory window (MW) of up to 20.6 V and a high endurance of 106. The stable 6-bit operation of our devices with 64 distinct states shows the feasibility of multilevel storage applications. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the FeFET in neuromorphic networks, with a high recognition accuracy of 93.02%.

items.title: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Molecular Biology, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan, ROC. mbhmli@gate.sinica.edu.tw.
items.abstract: Chloroplast protein-import channel Toc75 evolved from a cyanobacterial outer-membrane Omp85 protein, despite all known Omp85 proteins functioning in export. Chlamydomonas Toc75 assembles with Toc90M, the membrane-spanning domain of Toc90 (equivalent of higher-plant Toc159) into a binocular-shaped complex, but how this architecture arose and functions in import remain unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutational analysis of a cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal a lidded 16-β-strand barrel and three POTRA-domains involved in assembling outer-membrane proteins. Structural comparisons show that the Toc75-Toc90M complex mirrors an Omp85-substrate assembly intermediate, and Toc90M can indeed serve as a bacterial Omp85 substrate. While canonical Omp85 systems release substrates after assembly, Toc75 evolved a basic patch in its barrel to anchor Toc90M as a stable lateral pore through which precursor proteins are imported. Our findings indicate that a bacterial export system was converted into a chloroplast import channel by locking a substrate in place to provide an import conduit. This requirement for a stable assembly also supports that additional parts of the ancestral complex, including Omp85 POTRA-domains and Tic236 orthologs, were recruited to facilitate chloroplast protein import.

items.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy.
items.last_author_affiliation: Farber Institute for Neuroscience, Department of Neurology, Thomas Jefferson University, Philadelphia, PA, USA. joseph.tracy@jefferson.edu.
items.abstract: Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation.

items.title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Collaborative Innovation Center of Chemical Science and Engineering, Tianjin Key Laboratory of Applied Catalysis Science and Engineering, School of Chemical Engineering & Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China. xingang_li@tju.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Chemical Engineering and Low-Carbon Technology, Tianjin, China. xingang_li@tju.edu.cn.; Haihe Laboratory of Sustainable Chemical Transformations, Tianjin, China. xingang_li@tju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity-selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiOx overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h-1, exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis.

items.title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke.
items.last_author_affiliation: TRUTH Lab, School of Biomedical Engineering, ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China. chengbb@shanghaitech.edu.cn.; Shanghai Clinical Research and Trial Center, ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China. chengbb@shanghaitech.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Advanced Medical Materials and Devices, ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China. chengbb@shanghaitech.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO's clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders.

items.title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Computational Biology, University of Lausanne, Lausanne, Switzerland. zoltan.kutalik@unil.ch.; Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics (SIB), University of Lausanne, Lausanne, Switzerland. zoltan.kutalik@unil.ch.; University Center for Primary Care and Public Health, Lausanne, Switzerland. zoltan.kutalik@unil.ch.
items.abstract: Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual's known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase.Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual's observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE-ε4 status (linked with Alzheimer's disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10-4%, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE-ε4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited.

items.title: Single-atom-doped zeolite electrolyte for quasi-solid-state zinc-iodine batteries.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, National University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore. gzzhu@nus.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. Theoretical calculations, in situ spectroscopy, and laser confocal microscopy reveal that the single-atom metal sites enhance iodine conversion kinetics and suppress polyiodide shuttling through a synergistic catalytic-adsorption effect, with iron-doped zeolite exhibiting the strongest performance. Iron-doped zeolite further stabilizes water molecules, suppresses side reactions, and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The iron-doped zeolite-assembled zinc-iodine batteries maintain a discharge capacity of 81.2 mAh g-1 (based on iodine mass) after 6,800 cycles at 4 A g-1, while proof-of-concept pouch cells exhibit a capacity of 147.6 mAh g-1 (based on iodine mass) or 52 mAh g-1 (based on total positive electrode mass) after 200 cycles at 0.5 A g-1. Lastly, iron-doped zeolite also demonstrates compatibility with other positive electrode materials for rechargeable zinc batteries.

items.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Humanities & Social Sciences, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA, USA.
items.abstract: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability.

items.title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neurology, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. ding.jing@zs-hospital.sh.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Medical Neurobiology and MOE Frontiers Center for Brain Science, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. ding.jing@zs-hospital.sh.cn.
items.abstract: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy.

items.title: Arabian hydroclimate and hominin population dynamics over the last 500,000 years.
items.last_author_affiliation: Australian Research Centre for Human Evolution, Griffith University, Brisbane, QLD, Australia.; School of Social Science, University of Queensland, Brisbane, QLD, Australia.; Human Origins Program, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution, Washington, DC, USA.
items.abstract: Despite the discovery of a rich Palaeolithic archaeological record in Arabia over the last decade, the environmental context of hominin occupations and dispersals remains poorly understood owing to the paucity of Pleistocene palaeoenvironmental records. Here we show a multi-proxy, high-resolution dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean spanning the last 500,000 years, which enables evaluation of the influence of orbital-scale hydrological variations on hominin populations in Arabia. The dust evidence reinforces the view that hominin presence in Arabia was driven by enhanced monsoon precipitation during so-called Green Arabia periods. These results, coupled with hunter-gatherer demographic data, point to marked hominin population expansions during prolonged wetter periods. Hominin occupation, however, was not linked exclusively to traditional humid periods. Brief phases of high-intensity rainfall within some glacial periods, manifested by transient high dust contents associated with enhanced terrestrial moisture availability and increased supply of wind-erodible particles, also favoured hominin expansions.

items.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization.
items.last_author_affiliation: IBM Research, Cambridge, MA, USA. krotov@dynamicalmind.com.; Dynamical Mind, Cambridge, MA, USA. krotov@dynamicalmind.com.
items.abstract: Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

items.title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Urology, New York University Grossman School of Medicine, New York, 10016, NY, USA. xue-ru.wu@med.nyu.edu.; Veterans Affairs New York Harbor Healthcare System, Manhattan Campus, New York, 10010, NY, USA. xue-ru.wu@med.nyu.edu.; Department of Pathology, New York University School of Medicine, New York, 10016, NY, USA. xue-ru.wu@med.nyu.edu.
items.abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2-expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases.

items.title: One-shot synthesis of rare gastrointestinal lesions improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical training.
items.last_author_affiliation: Centre for AI and Decision Sciences, Alliance Manchester Business School, The University of Manchester, Manchester, UK. xian.yang@manchester.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Rare gastrointestinal lesions are infrequently encountered in routine endoscopy, limiting data for developing reliable artificial intelligence (AI) models and training novice clinicians. Here we present EndoRare, a one-shot, retraining-free generative framework that synthesizes diverse lesion exemplars from a single reference image. Using language-guided concept disentanglement, EndoRare separates pathognomonic lesion features from non-diagnostic attributes, encoding the former into a learnable prototype embedding while varying the latter to ensure diversity. We validate EndoRare across four rare pathologies: calcifying fibrous tumor, juvenile polyposis syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Experts judge the synthetic images clinically plausible, and data augmentation significantly improves downstream AI classifiers, increasing true positive rates at low false-positive rates. In an exploratory reader study, exposure to EndoRare-generated cases is associated with improved image-level recognition by novice endoscopists. These findings support the potential use of EndoRare as a data-efficient tool for rare-lesion education and motivate prospective controlled validation.

items.title: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Cardiology, Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine; Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Cardiovascular Intervention and Precision Medicine; Engineering Research Center for Cardiovascular Innovative Devices of Zhejiang Province, Hangzhou, China. 3313011@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The adult heart has limited regenerative capacity after ischemic injury, and abnormal fatty acid metabolism contributes to this failure of repair. Strategies that reduce fatty acid oxidation can promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, but excessive suppression may disrupt lipid handling and worsen injury. Here we show that a platelet-engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery system enables targeted suppression of the fatty acid transporter CD36 and promotes cardiac repair after ischemia-reperfusion injury. By using platelets as injury-responsive carriers, the system preferentially accumulates in damaged myocardium, reduces neutralization by circulating antibodies, and enhances cardiac delivery of the therapeutic vector. In a male mouse model, CD36 knockdown reduces fatty acid utilization, reshapes cardiac lipid metabolism without causing overt lipid overload, increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, and improves cardiac structure and function. These findings establish a platelet-guided gene delivery strategy that links metabolic reprogramming to myocardial regeneration and suggest a promising approach for ischemic heart repair.

items.title: Label-free, real-time optical biopsy with a handheld quantitative phase microscope.
items.last_author_affiliation: Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology and Emory University, Atlanta, GA, USA. francisco.robles@stjude.org.; Winship Cancer Institute, Emory University, Atlanta, GA, USA. francisco.robles@stjude.org.; Department of Imaging Sciences, St Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis, TN, USA. francisco.robles@stjude.org.
items.abstract: We present a compact, handheld quantitative phase imaging microscope that enables label-free, real-time optical imaging of bulk tissues with clear cellular and subcellular histological detail, effectively providing an "optical biopsy." The approach uses quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) to obtain quantitative phase information of opaque samples using epi-illumination. The probe has a wide-field, non-scanning architecture that achieves 0.8 µm lateral and 5 µm axial resolution across a 300 µm × 300 µm field of view at 25 frames per second. The probe is also low-cost, contains no moving components, is easy to use and can operate through a sterile sheath, addressing key barriers to clinical implementation. To demonstrate its utility, we image (1) human skin in vivo, (2) murine and human brain tumors ex vivo, and (3) swine brain in vivo under typical neurosurgical conditions. By providing real-time, label-free histological information in a robust and accessible handheld format, this technology creates broad opportunities for future clinical translation, including intraoperative and point-of-care histological tissue assessment.

items.title: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy: a phase II clinical randomized trial.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Anesthesiology, The Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, China. caojl0310@aliyun.com.; Jiangsu Province Key Laboratory of Anesthesia and Brain Science & Jiangsu Province Key Laboratory of Anesthesiology, Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, China. caojl0310@aliyun.com.
items.abstract: Perioperative liver injury is a common complication following partial hepatectomy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. Preclinical studies have shown that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has hepatoprotective effects, but clinical evidence remains limited. This study is a phase II, prospective, double-blind, randomized trial involving 140 patients undergoing partial hepatectomy, in which the active-taVNS group received 60-minute stimulation sessions at four time points: during the first hepatic pedicle clamping, after extubation in the post-anesthesia care unit, and on postoperative days 1 and 2 between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM. The primary outcome measure was serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels on postoperative day 2. Results showed that the median ALT level in the active taVNS group was significantly lower than that in the sham stimulation group (144.5 U/L vs. 224.0 U/L; P = 0.002). The results suggest that taVNS may have an early and transient protective effect against hepatocellular injury, providing preliminary clinical evidence for its potential as a non-invasive intervention strategy for early liver damage following partial hepatectomy. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092005).
items.type: Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial

items.title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center of Excellence for Data-Driven Discovery, Department of Structural Biology, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis, TN, USA. madan.babu@stjude.org.; Department of Structural Biology, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis, TN, USA. madan.babu@stjude.org.; Office of Data Science, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis, TN, USA. madan.babu@stjude.org.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including "relevance scores" and "hallucination index," and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

items.title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort.
items.last_author_affiliation: Variant Bio, Seattle, WA, USA. stephane@variantbio.com.
items.abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations.
