Treatment was associated with broad remodeling of the plasma proteome and metabolome, but the extent to which this remodeling depended on weight loss differed across the molecular layers. The metabolome carried a lipid signature that scaled with the weight lost, whereas proteomic and inflammation-panel changes largely did not depend on weight loss. Among these changes, treatment was associated with lower circulating mitochondrial oxidative proteins and cardiolipins, consistent with relief of lipid-driven metabolic stress, and with a shift of the inflammation panel toward a less inflamed state. A metabolic aging clock showed that age acceleration decreased by a mean of 2.96 years after treatment (95% confidence interval -4.95 to -0.98; P = 3.7 x 10-3), a change that did not depend on weight loss or on the interval between samples, with the largest reductions in participants starting from the highest age acceleration, most of whom had diabetes. Treatment-associated features overlapped with features associated with cardiometabolic, renal and hepatic disease. Before treatment, higher systemic inflammation, reflecting chronic tissue stress and repair, was associated with less subsequent weight loss. Together, these findings indicate that incretin agonist treatment is associated with lower markers of metabolic and inflammatory stress and with a younger metabolic age, changes that do not depend on weight loss, identify baseline inflammation as an axis of heterogeneity in treatment response, and suggest that biorepositories linking longitudinal multi-omic profiling to clinical records can relate drug pharmacodynamics to disease risk and to variation in patient response.

items.title: An information theoretic approach to evaluating social behaviour in mice using automated home-cage monitoring
items.abstract: Background: Social behaviour in mice is commonly assessed using standardized assays such as the three-chambered task, which provide controlled measures of sociability but often capture behaviour over short timeframes that may not capture the complex behavioural repertoire exhibited in the home environment. Although automated home-cage monitoring enables continuous, longitudinal assessment of group-housed mice with minimal human interference, methods for quantifying social behaviour in this complex setting remain limited. Information theory offers a framework for measuring statistical dependence between animals but requires one to account for dependence related to the cage environment that arise even in the absence of social interaction. Methods: We developed an information-theoretic approach to quantify social dependence using longitudinal RFID-based positional data from group-housed mice monitored with automated home-cage monitoring system. Mutual information (MI) between cagemates was evaluated against a constrained null model that disrupted within-cage dependence while preserving individual movement patterns. We used two strains with known differences in sociability (C57BL/6J and BTBR) to assess sensitivity to various temporal sampling parameters, test-retest reliability, and correspondence with manually video-scored social behaviours. We further examined variation across genetic backgrounds and investigated relationships between home-cage measures, conventional behavioural assays (three-chamber sociability and open-field behaviour), and brain structure using in vivo MRI. Results: Observed MI was distinguishable from our null distribution, validating its use to quantify statistical dependence beyond that expected from shared cage constraints. MI recapitulated known differences in sociability between C57BL/6J and BTBR mice, showed high test-retest reliability, and correlated with independently video-scored social behaviours. Home-cage social measures also varied across genetic backgrounds and captured strain differences separate from three-chamber sociability. Furthermore, in vivo MRI revealed distinct neuroanatomical patterns for home cage compared to three-chamber sociability measures, including brain regions implicated in social behaviour. Comparisons with open-field measures further indicated that home-cage information-theoretic measures capture behavioural variation not fully represented by conventional measures of locomotion and exploration. Finally, social coordination exhibited distinct temporal dynamics across the circadian cycle. Conclusion: This study establishes and validates an information-theoretic framework for quantifying social dependence from longitudinal home-cage positional data. By accounting for dependence arising from shared environmental constraints and demonstrating reproducibility and correspondence with observed social behaviour, this approach provides a complementary method for characterizing social behaviour in mice. Its application across genetic backgrounds and temporal contexts offers opportunities to investigate behavioural variation beyond the restricted sampling of conventional assays.

items.title: Sex differences in the effects of enhanced adult hippocampal neurogenesis on pattern discrimination and Intellicage spatial learning in Bax-knockout mice
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurosciences, University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center
items.abstract: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis has been implicated in learning and memory. Although increasing neurogenesis has been associated with improved spatial learning and pattern discrimination, whether these benefits differ between male and female mice remains unclear. The goal of this study was to see if increasing adult hippocampal neurogenesis improves learning in male and female mice, and whether the benefit is the same in both sexes. We used conditional deletion of the pro-apoptotic gene Bax to increase the survival of newborn dentate granule cells. Male and female BAX knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) mice were tested in Intellicage place learning and reversal learning tasks, and an A/B context discrimination task. BAX KO mice had more tdTomato-positive newborn dentate granule cells than BAX WT mice, with no significant effect of sex. During Intellicage adaptation, there were no differences between genotypes or sexes in total visits and licks. During place learning, male mice had a higher percent correct response than female mice, while female mice showed increases in licks and correct visits from day 1 to day 4. BAX KO mice made more visits overall but had a lower percent correct response than BAX WT mice on day 4. During reversal learning, male BAX KO mice showed a decrease in visits and had fewer visits with a lick than male BAX WT mice on day 4. In the A/B task, male BAX KO mice had higher discrimination scores than male BAX WT mice on day 5, while female BAX KO mice showed an initial advantage over female BAX WT mice. These results partially support our hypothesis that increasing neurogenesis would benefit male mice more. Overall, increasing the survival of newborn dentate granule cells does not improve learning in the same way across sexes and tasks.

items.title: Sympathetic-to-microglia readouts in human brain single-nucleus data: sparse adrenergic receptor detection and age-associated homeostatic-to-inflammatory shifts in hippocampal microglia
items.corresponding_institution: First affiliated hospital of Fujian Medical University
items.abstract: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) improves sleep in clinical populations, yet the mechanisms linking sympathetic activity to human microglial states remain untested. A prerequisite is to establish what sympathetic signaling readouts exist in human microglia and whether state composition changes in a disease-relevant physiological dimension. Using two public human single-nucleus datasets (the ROSMAP prefrontal cortex resource: 443 donors, 174,420 immune nuclei, 152,459 microglial nuclei, 12 published microglial states; and a hippocampal multiome cohort spanning adult lifespan: 40 donors, ages 20 - 100, 15,225 microglial nuclei), we quantified (i) adrenergic receptor and inflammatory/complement axis gene expression across microglial states, and (ii) donor-level trajectories of four microglial state signatures across age. Adrenergic receptors were barely detected: among nine receptor genes, only ADRB2 was detectable in 3.8 - 11.4% of nuclei, and no adrenergic receptor was state-specific. In contrast, inflammatory genes (nuclear factor-{kappa}B and interleukin modules) were strongly concentrated in one pro-inflammatory state (e.g., NFKB1 mean expression 1.47 vs 0.35 - 0.72 in other states; IL1B in 32.6% of nuclei vs 2 - 16% elsewhere), complement genes in a complement-enriched state, and lipid-metabolism/disease-associated genes in a distinct state. Across the adult lifespan, hippocampal microglia showed a donor-level decline of the homeostatic signature (mean score 0.70 to 0.38 across age quartiles; Spearman {rho} = -0.55, P = 2.6 * 10-4), with concordant rises of pro-inflammatory ({rho} = 0.37, P = 0.017) and disease-associated/lipid-metabolism ({rho} = 0.32, P = 0.045) signatures; an interferon signature showed no age trend. These results (a) indicate that human microglia lack a robust direct adrenergic receptor substrate at single-nucleus resolution, implying that sympathetic influence on microglia, if causal, is likely indirect or low-frequency, and (b) establish a donor-level, age-associated baseline shift toward inflammatory/trimming states in the human hippocampus. Together they define candidate readouts and the baseline against which chronic-sleep-disorder and neuromodulation-intervention studies (e.g., SGB) should be designed.

items.title: Target- and network-specific downstream effects of personalized precision transcranial magnetic stimulation: Evidence from concurrent functional neuroimaging
items.corresponding_institution: Leibniz Institute for Resilience Research (LIR), Mainz, Germany
items.abstract: Background: Personalized targeting of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) based on functional connectivity (FC) to the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) is promising for depression treatment, but direct evidence that precisely engaging an individually defined FC target produces specific downstream modulation is lacking. Objective: To test whether stimulating individually defined cortical targets with strong negative or positive FC to sgACC/ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) produces target- and network-specific downstream BOLD effects compared to nearby control targets. Methods: Twenty healthy participants underwent concurrent TMS-fMRI. For each participant, we identified a dorsolateral PFC target with strong negative FC and a dorsomedial PFC target with strong positive FC to sgACC/vmPFC as well as control targets with weaker sgACC/vmPFC-FC strength, but matched peripheral co-stimulation experience. Coil positions and orientations were optimized using electric field simulations. Single TMS pulses were applied during concurrent fMRI, and BOLD responses were compared between conditions. Results: Stimulation of negative FC targets produced significantly stronger negative BOLD modulation in sgACC/vmPFC and dorsomedial PFC compared to control targets. Positive FC targets showed no significant differences from controls. The spatial pattern of negative FC target-related BOLD effects significantly resembled a previously described convergent depression circuit, while positive FC targets produced an anticorrelated pattern. Conclusions: Personalized precision TMS targeting produces target- and network-specific downstream effects, supporting the mechanistic premise of FC-guided TMS.

items.title: Hierarchical control of visual perceptual learning with model-synthesized stimuli
items.abstract: Visual perceptual decisions depend on both how the visual system represents the stimuli and how those representations are read out to guide perception and behavior. Improved visual perception through training, a phenomenon known as Visual Perceptual Learning (VPL), has been partly attributed to adjustments of the readout weights across visual areas to reach better decisions. However, it has been difficult to test whether this reweighting remains at a late stage of the hierarchy or can amplify the readout of whichever hierarchical stage has the most informative representations for the training stimulus. Here, we leveraged DorsalNet, a hierarchical neural network model of the primate dorsal stream, to synthesize motion stimuli that selectively target early or late areas of the primate dorsal pathway. Human observers were trained to discriminate the synthesized stimuli over three days, and transfer was subsequently measured across retinal location and stimulus type. Training improved performance for both stimulus types (early- and late-stage targeting stimuli), but through different mechanisms. Training with late-stage stimuli significantly increased perceptual sensitivity, a gain that transferred across retinal locations. Training with early-stage stimuli produced only a weak, non-significant change in sensitivity; instead, it significantly reduced a conservative response bias, an effect that did not persist at the new retinal location. Specificity indices for stimulus location and type showed different patterns across stimulus categories. A DorsalNet-based model of VPL reproduced both the learning dynamics and these distinct specificity patterns most closely when the model readout was solely plastic for late, rather than early, model layers. Together, these results support a late-stage reweighting account of perceptual learning, in which readout from a preferred, late stage of the dorsal hierarchy is reweighted regardless of the trained stimulus. Under this account, stimuli well matched to the readout stage yield sensitivity gains, whereas poorly matched stimuli afford only weak sensory evidence, prompting observers to compensate by shifting their decision criteria.

items.title: Novel Stable 5-OP-RU Analogs Activate Human MAIT Cells and Promote Cytotoxic Antitumor Function
items.abstract: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are abundant innate-like T lymphocytes that recognize microbial vitamin B2-derived metabolites presented by MR1 and play pivotal roles in infection, autoimmunity, and cancer. Pharmacologic activation with 5-OP-RU, 5-(2 oxopropylideneamino)-D-ribityl-aminouracil potently stimulates MAIT cells and elicits antitumor immune responses, but its intrinsic chemical instability limits therapeutic development. Here, we designed and evaluated novel synthetic 5-OP-RU analogs to improve stability and assess their potential for MAIT directed anti-tumor immunity. Selected analogs induced surface MR1 upregulation and expanded MAIT cells in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy donors and patients with liver cancer. Analog stimulation promoted perforin and granzyme B expression, inflammatory cytokine release, and tumor-cell killing by MAIT-enriched populations in vitro. Structure-activity analysis identified chemical modifications that preserved agonist activity, with several cyclic analogs showing improved chemical and metabolic stability. The series also yielded compounds that upregulated MR1 but inhibited 5-OP-RU-induced MAIT expansion, consistent with antagonist activity. Initial pharmacokinetic studies showed distinct plasma and hepatic exposure profiles in mice. In an orthotopic liver cancer model, select analogs administered with CpG reduced tumor burden and increased hepatic MAIT cell frequency. These findings establish a chemical biology framework for developing stable isolable MAIT ligands as next-generation MAIT-directed cancer immunotherapies.

items.title: DNA Methyltransferase Inhibition During CAR T-cell Manufacturing Enhances Antitumor Activity in Immunocompetent Brain and Ovarian Cancer Models
items.corresponding_institution: Children's National Hospital, Center for Cancer and Immunology Research Washington, DC, US
items.abstract: Limited persistence and progressive dysfunction remain major barriers to effective CAR T-cell therapy for solid tumors. Epigenetic regulation, particularly DNA methylation, can reinforce dysfunctional T-cell programs by restricting expression of genes required for sustained effector function. CAR T-cell manufacturing provides an opportunity to pharmacologically prime CAR T-cells prior to infusion without additional treatment burden. Therefore, we hypothesized that transient DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) inhibition during CAR T-cell manufacturing would epigenetically modulate CAR T-cell state and enhance functional and antitumor activity against solid tumors. We evaluated transient DNMT inhibition during ex vivo murine CAR T-cell manufacturing using two mechanistically distinct compounds: the nucleoside analogue 5-azacytidine (5-Aza) and the selective DNMT1 inhibitor GSK3685032 (GSK). Epigenetic and transcriptomic profiling, together with functional analyses including repeated antigen stimulation, were performed to characterize the molecular and functional effects of DNMT inhibition on CAR T-cells. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in immunocompetent syngeneic murine models of pediatric glioma and ovarian cancer by assessing tumor burden and survival. 5-Aza treatment induced dose-dependent epigenetic and transcriptional changes in CAR T-cells that were accompanied by enhanced expansion, sustained cytotoxicity and cytokine production during repeated antigen challenge in vitro. These improvements translated in vivo, with enhanced tumor control across immunocompetent models of high-grade glioma, diffuse midline glioma, and ovarian cancer using both B7-H3- and GD2-targeting CAR constructs. The dose associated with the greatest benefit varied by CAR construct and tumor model. In contrast, selective DNMT1 inhibition with GSK did not recapitulate the molecular or functional benefits of 5-Aza and reduced therapeutic efficacy in vivo. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that transient epigenetic modulation during CAR T-cell manufacturing can durably reshape CAR T-cell state and enhance antitumor efficacy. Broad DNMT inhibition with 5-Aza produced molecular, functional, and therapeutic benefits that were distinct from selective DNMT1 inhibition with GSK. These results support transient 5-Aza treatment during manufacturing as a translatable strategy to improve CAR T-cell therapies for solid tumors.

items.title: Distinct monocyte replenishment kinetics of macrophages at the oral barrier restrict early-life bacterial colonisation
items.abstract: Resident tissue macrophages (RTMs) support tissue integrity and homeostasis. However, RTM in the gingiva, the mucosal barrier surrounding the teeth and the site of the prevalent inflammatory disease periodontitis, remain minimally explored. The gingiva experiences a unique combination of challenges, it is continuously exposed to both microbial stimuli and mastication-induced tissue damage; RTM could provide barrier reinforcement against both these challenges. Here we outline that no long-lived macrophage population could be identified within the gingiva. We demonstrate that gingiva macrophages are continuously replenished at a rate not impacted by the considerable microbial burden at this site. Despite microbe-induced signalling failing to determine macrophage replenishment, these signals did play key roles in re-shaping the macrophage network in early-life. We show that microbial-signals drive early-life increases in gingiva macrophages which are transient but vital to restrict the growth of the oral commensal community. Combined, our study delineates the biology of gingiva macrophages across life, outlining a developmentally restricted window during which these cells play key roles in regulating microbial colonisation.

items.title: A B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis contributes to myocarditis induced by checkpoint blockade and cardiac irradiation
items.abstract: Thoracic radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve outcomes in locally advanced lung cancer but can cause cardiac toxicity. The mechanisms by which radiation-associated cardiac injury develops into autoimmune myocarditis during ICI therapy remain incompletely defined. Using autoimmune-prone A/J mice, we investigated whether cardiac irradiation (CIR) promotes a B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis during dual PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade. Dual ICIs plus CIR increased the incidence of myocarditis to 76.2% and cardiac fibrosis to 69.0%. CIR did not further increase global splenic B-cell activation beyond dual ICIs alone but increased cardiac troponin I-reactive B cells and IgG, circulating cardiac autoantibodies (cAAbs), myocardial IgG accumulation, and C3/C3a activation. In mice subsequently found to have grade 3-4 myocarditis on day 21, cAAbs increased by day 7 and continued to rise, preceding histologic identification of severe disease. Cobra venom factor-mediated C3 depletion reduced myocarditis incidence from 90% to 40% and fibrosis from 85% to 35%, while also decreasing B-cell activation and circulating cAAbs. In a separate LLC-OVA tumor model, C3 depletion did not produce an evident loss of the antitumor activity of combined ICIs and radiation under the conditions tested. These findings support a model in which CIR focuses ICI-associated humoral immunity toward cardiac antigens and complement amplifies cardiac injury. The early cAAb rise and protection achieved by C3 depletion provide a rationale for prospective evaluation of cAAbs as a risk marker and complement signaling as a therapeutic target.

items.title: Intradermal and intranasal vaccination with microparticulated ASFV proteins induces distinct immune profiles in pigs
items.abstract: African Swine Fever (ASF) is a major threat to the swine industry due to its severe socioeconomic impact and the lack of safe and effective vaccines. Although live attenuated vaccines (LAVs) can induce robust immunity, biosafety concerns restrict their use, making subunit vaccines the preferred alternative. In this context, understanding how vaccination routes modulate immunity is critical. A previous study using a viral vector-based vaccine, encoding for the ASFV antigens p30, p54, p72, p72c and CD2v, induced protection when combining intranasal (IN) and parenteral administrations. However, the relative contribution of each administration route to vaccine-induced immunity remains unclear. Here we investigated how independent and combined vaccination routes influence the immune responses induced by the same ASFV protein cocktail delivered as nanoparticle-based secretory granules. Following a prime-boost regime, pigs vaccinated via intradermal (ID) route seroconverted and developed strong systemic ASFV-specific IgG responses, despite inducing only modest ASFV-specific cellular responses. In contrast, IN administration alone failed to elicit detectable systemic humoral or cellular responses and did not improve the vaccine-induced immunogenicity when combined with the ID route. Following a challenge with a virulent ASFV strain, no protection was achieved in any of the immunized groups. Interestingly, intranasally vaccinated pigs exhibited an accelerated post-challenge ASFV-specific antibody boost in serum compared to controls, suggesting that vaccination through this mucosal route induced immune priming despite the absence of detectable systemic humoral responses before challenge. Overall, these findings reveal distinct route-dependent immune profiles elicited by the same ASFV antigen cocktail and highlight again that robust humoral responses alone are insufficient for protection, further supporting the importance of cellular immunity in vaccine-induced protection.

items.title: Human eIF3 and eIF5 coordinate AUG recognition to sustain energy homeostasis
items.abstract: Precise translation initiation is essential for efficient production of proteins; missing or mis-selecting the canonical start site can have detrimental consequences. Past research identified several initiation factors governing start codon selection accuracy in yeast, but the increasing complexity of higher eukaryotes have limited similar research in mammalian cells. We present an in cellulo study of knock-in mutants of the eIF3c subunit of the multitasking eIF3 complex that disrupt eIF3's interaction with eIF5, thereby preventing functional binding of eIF5 to pre-initiation complexes. This selectively relaxes start site selection stringency and reduces initiation sensitivity, leading to altered translation efficiency for nearly 600 proteins. Proteins with N-terminal targeting signals were among those especially affected, resulting in impaired mitochondrial function. These findings establish the first direct causal link between an initiation factor, stringent start site recognition, and impaired mitochondrial respiration and glycolytic activity, implicating the eIF3-eIF5 interaction as a key regulator of energy homeostasis.

items.title: LUBAC ubiquitinates FADD and Caspase-8 through distinct catalytic mechanisms and limits TNF-induced apoptosis
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas at Austin
items.abstract: The linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) is a critical regulator of tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling that promotes pro-survival responses and suppresses apoptosis. Linear ubiquitination of the TNFR1-associated complex II components FADD and Caspase-8 has been reported, but whether they are direct LUBAC substrates, how they are modified, and what the modification does remain poorly understood. Here, we show that loss of HOIP, which destabilizes the LUBAC complex, sensitizes HCT116 cells to TNF-induced apoptosis, and that TNF induces linear ubiquitin-reactive species on endogenous FADD and Caspase-8. Using purified proteins, we demonstrate that FADD and Caspase-8 are direct LUBAC substrates with different catalytic requirements. Efficient FADD ubiquitination requires HOIL-1L in addition to HOIP, consistent with a priming-and-extension mechanism, whereas Caspase-8 is ubiquitinated by HOIP-containing subcomplexes lacking HOIL-1L. A complex containing FADD, Caspase-8, and RIPK1 formed independently of LUBAC activity, but pharmacological inhibition of HOIP increased Caspase-8 processing within the FADD-associated pool, and Met1-ubiquitinated FADD showed reduced binding to Caspase-8 in vitro. Mapping identified four death domain lysines that each support LUBAC-dependent FADD ubiquitination. In FADD-deficient cells, a FADD-diubiquitin fusion attenuated TNF/cycloheximide-induced apoptosis relative to wild-type FADD, whereas a lysine-less FADD supported apoptosis with delayed kinetics. Together, these findings identify FADD and Caspase-8 as direct LUBAC substrates modified through distinct catalytic routes and support a model in which ubiquitination of FADD limits productive engagement with Caspase-8.

items.title: Protease shaving resolves the surface proteome of infection-derived extracellular vesicles and unmasks their inflammatory activity
items.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) produced and released by infected macrophages carry both host proteins and bacterial antigens, but whether these components face outward, are enclosed within vesicles, or are associated with co-isolated material remains unclear, limiting our understanding of their accessibility to recipient cells. We combined proteinase K shaving with quantitative proteomics to characterize the protease-accessible proteome of sEVs released by Salmonella-infected RAW264.7 macrophages. Host and bacterial proteins exhibited distinct responses to proteolysis. Of 1,368 proteins quantified, 246 were significantly decreased following digestion and a further 93 became undetectable. Among the depleted proteins, 26 carried independent topological evidence of surface exposure, spanning tetraspanins, integrins, MHC class I molecules, GPI-anchored proteins and membrane receptors, and the depleted fraction also included the immune mediators TNF-, CSF2RA, CD40 and MIF. Most detected Salmonella proteins resisted proteolysis and seven were significantly increased. Peptide-level analysis localized TNF- depletion to its extracellular domain, which fell by more than 3 log? relative to a cytoplasmic peptide measured in the same injection. Preservation of luminal sEV markers and two normalization-independent measures indicated that vesicle integrity was maintained. Despite removal of this protease-accessible fraction, vesicle bioactivity was not diminished: proteinase K-treated vesicles induced stronger Il6 expression and NF-{kappa}B/AP-1 signaling than untreated vesicles, with both responses sensitive to TNF- blockade and polymyxin B. Our findings together suggest that the protease-accessible protein fraction influences the immunostimulatory activity of infection-derived sEV preparations, with removal of the externally available coat of EVs being associated with enhanced inflammatory signaling.

items.title: Electrophysiological Comparison of Mechanosensitive PIEZO1 Channel Currents across Different Human Cell Types
items.abstract: The detection of mechanical stress is essential for a wide range of physiological functions in humans, including touch sensation, hearing, and the maintenance of vascular myogenic tone. PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive cation channel that is widely expressed in both neuronal and non-neuronal cells and plays critical physiological roles in multiple organs. However, the electrophysiological properties of endogenous PIEZO1-mediated mechanosensitive currents have not been systematically compared across different human cell types under identical experimental conditions. Here, the author compared the electrophysiological properties of endogenous human PIEZO1 (hPIEZO1) currents in four cultured human cell types: human aortic endothelial cells, human brain capillary endothelial cells, human fibroblast-like synoviocytes, and human osteoblast-like MG63 cells. Under whole-cell patch-clamp conditions, application of the PIEZO1 agonist Yoda1 robustly activated hPIEZO1-like currents in all four cell types. In excised outside-out patch recordings, application of positive pressure to membrane patches from these cells also elicited PIEZO1-like channel currents, which were markedly potentiated by Yoda1 and effectively inhibited by gadolinium, a non-selective cation channel blocker. Furthermore, the unitary current amplitudes of single channel events evoked by mechanical stimulation were comparable to those elicited by Yoda1 across all four cell types. Collectively, these findings provide electrophysiological evidence that endogenous PIEZO1 functions as a mechanosensor in diverse human cell types and suggest that PIEZO1 contributes to mechanically regulated physiological processes in multiple human organs.

items.title: Identification of ATAD1 at Mitochondria-ER Contact Sites Reveals Its Role in Mitochondrial-to-ER Protein Transfer
items.abstract: Mitochondria-ER contact sites (MERCs) play important roles in cellular functions such as lipid and Ca2+ transport and the regulation of mitochondrial dynamics. To better understand the functional diversity of MERCs, it is critical to identify proteins localized at these sites. Here, we employed CsFiND (Complementation assay using fusion of Split-GFP and TurboID) to identify MERC-associated proteins in HeLa cells. Proteomic and cell biological analyses identified ATAD1, a mitochondrial AAA-ATPase, as a MERC-associated protein. ATAD1 facilitates the transfer of GFP-Pex26{triangleup}C, a mislocalized peroxisomal membrane protein, from mitochondria to the ER. GFP-Pex26{triangleup}C is then degraded by the proteasome in a manner dependent on the ER-resident E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCH6. Notably, proteasome inhibition resulted in the accumulation of GFP-Pex26{triangleup}C at MERCs, suggesting that these sites may participate in this quality-control pathway. Together, these findings suggest a potential role for MERCs in the quality control of proteins mislocalized to mitochondria.

items.title: Targeted protein depletion in quiescent fission yeast cells using an auxin-degron system
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Biochemistry and Cellular Genetics, CNRS UMR 5095
items.abstract: Quiescence is a reversible, non-proliferative cellular state in which cells can remain for extended periods of time while retaining the ability to re-enter the cell cycle upon exposure to favorable conditions. This physiological state is critical for a broad range of biological processes, from stress response in unicellular systems to differentiation and development in multicellular organisms. Surprisingly, despite its recognized roles in cell biology in diverse species, key aspects of the regulation of quiescence remain poorly understood. To investigate protein function specifically in quiescence, a conditional activation approach is critical, in particular for factors that are essential for cell viability. However, the efficacy of a number of such inactivation strategies in quiescent cells remained unknown. Using nitrogen-depleted fission yeast cells as a well-established model for quiescence, we probed two types of commonly-used approaches: a targeted method for the reversible inhibition of engineered kinases using non-hydrolyzable ATP analogs, and a more general system targeting protein depletion using an auxin-inducible degron. Here we show that the use of analog-sensitive kinases is unsuitable for quiescent fission yeast cells, as the ATP analog serves as a nitrogen source and induces cell cycle re-entry. We then demonstrate how coupling a degron tag with a specific auxin ligand allows for rapid, lasting and reversible protein depletion in quiescent cells, providing a powerful tool for investigating the regulation of this crucial and widespread cellular state.

items.title: Phosphorylation of the ER-plasma membrane tether E-Syt2 facilitates the loss of contact sites in mitosis
items.abstract: Mitosis is associated with dramatic remodeling of intracellular organelles that supports their equal distribution between daughter cells. Recent investigations into membrane contact sites (MCS) show that they also remodel in mitosis with a significant loss of ER-plasma membrane CS (ERPMCS). However, the mechanisms governing this loss are unknown. Here we show that phosphorylation of the ERPMCS tether extended synaptotagmin 2 (E-Syt2) facilitates the loss of ERPMCS in mitosis. Preventing E-Syt2 phosphorylation in mitosis rescues the loss of ERPMCS. The persistence of ERPMCS is associated with delayed growth and progression through mitosis. This shows that E-Syt2 mitosis specific phosphorylation regulates its tethering potential and that the loss of ERPMCS is important for timely cell division.

items.title: Beyond Abundance: Integrated Splicing and Expression Quantitative Trait Loci Refine Causal Gene Mapping in IBD
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Genetics, School of Medicine, The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, NC, USA
items.abstract: Splicing quantitative trait loci (sQTL) remain less explored than expression QTL (eQTL) in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We mapped cis-eQTL and cis-sQTL in 1,149 colon samples from SPARC IBD participants in IBD Plexus, identifying 20,566 genes with eQTL (eGenes) and 9,906 with sQTL (sGenes). Colocalization prioritized 239 eGenes and 164 sGenes across 147 of 320 IBD risk loci, including 58 genes supported by both traits. We assessed candidate splicing consequences involving nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), 5' untranslated region remodeling, and protein domain alteration. In five genes with GWAS-colocalized eQTL and sQTL, risk alleles were associated with reciprocal changes in total gene expression and usage of junctions linked to predicted NMD-sensitive transcripts, consistent with NMD. IBD-associated sGenes were enriched in immune and inflammatory pathways and included drug targets. These findings motivate investigation of whether genotype-associated splicing differences, particularly those predicted to alter protein domains, contribute to variation in responses to IBD therapies.

items.title: Multi-resolution QTL mapping in four interconnected rice RIL populations reveals recurrent, background-specific, and environment-dependent loci
authors: Prado, J. F. F. d. S.
items.abstract: We aimed to determine how marker density influences the detection and localization of quantitative trait loci (QTLs) in rice and to identify parental alleles with consistent effects across genetic backgrounds and environments. We evaluated grain yield, plant height, and flowering time in four interconnected recombinant inbred line populations at two Brazilian sites, Goianira and Boa Vista. Each parent contributed to two crosses, allowing us to compare the direction of its allelic effects in different genetic backgrounds. We compared a common backbone of 2,060 DArTseq SNPs with denser, cross-specific panels using marker and bin regression, interval mapping based on genotype probabilities inferred by hidden Markov models, and genome-wide permutation thresholds. The backbone recovered the major QTL regions. Peak positions differed by less than 100 kb in 14 of 19 comparisons within crosses and environments, including five exact matches. Across the four maps, densification increased marker counts 4.66-fold and recombination bin counts 2.44-fold. Recombination-breakpoint interval width decreased by 31.1% in Maninjau/Epagri 108 and 90.3% in Irat 122/Araguaia. Comparisons using the same lines resolved an apparent peak shift at qPH12 and placed qYLD2 below the genome-wide threshold in both panels. Four QTL regions recurred across crosses. Epagri 108 contributed all of them for reduced height at qPH1, whose interval contains SD1, and delayed flowering at qDTH8. Araguaia contributed an allele for earlier flowering at qDTH3 in both its crosses. The qDTH6 region recurred in Goianira, and the opposite flowering effects observed across environments in Irat 122/Araguaia mapped to different chromosome 6 peaks. Grain-yield QTLs showed less recurrence. The strongest associations, qYLD1 and qYLD6, occurred in separate indica/japonica crosses. In Goianira, qYLD6 explained 32.5% of phenotypic variance in the full-panel analysis and achieved genome-wide significance only at that site. Parental genome sequences helped prioritize candidate genes. Two complementary recombinants delimited a 247.0-kb region containing Ef-cd at qDTH3, while Hd1 and OsCLF remained genetically unresolved within a 51.8-kb marker-defined interval at qDTH6. These findings identify Epagri 108/Araguaia as a candidate cross for combining reduced height with earlier flowering. For grain yield, the favorable Maninjau allele at qYLD1 and Epagri 108 allele at qYLD6 warrant testing individually and together in recipient backgrounds under target growing conditions. Because the backbone was derived retrospectively, its economic benefit requires prospective evaluation. For routine marker-assisted selection, breeders could genotype founders and initial mapping families at high density, use a common panel of markers representing recombination bins to track validated haplotypes across subsequent families, and add cross-specific flanking markers to select progeny that retain a favorable allele within a smaller donor segment.

items.title: A refined InDel taxonomy broadens the repertoire of mutational processes shaping multiple myeloma
items.corresponding_institution: Sylvester Myeloma Institute, Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, University of Miami, Miami, FL, United States
items.abstract: Somatic aberrations have been extensively characterized in multiple myeloma (MM). However, the mutational processes underlying small insertions and deletions (InDels) remain poorly understood. Here, we used a recently developed 89-channel InDel classification schema which allows differentiating mutational processes. We analyzed whole-genome sequencing data from 887 MM samples, spanning both newly diagnosed (NDMM) and relapsed/refractory disease (RRMM). We identified InDel signatures associated with replication slippage, APOBEC mutagenesis, topoisomerase 1 (TOP1)-mediated mutagenesis, non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), and two rare DNA damage repair-deficiency signatures. In two randomized clinical trials, incorporation of the APOBEC InDel signature InD9a improved treatment outcome prediction as pertaining to progression-free survival (PFS) and achievement of minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity. InD29, a signature linked to NHEJ-mediated errors, was detected in both NDMM and RRMM, and was enriched in samples exhibiting melphalan-associated mutagenesis and high SV burden. Genome-wide analysis identified a recurrent InDel hotspot at TXNDC5, a highly expressed gene in MM located within a region implicated in complex genomic rearrangements, with predominantly noncoding alterations suggesting potential regulatory consequences. Finally, InDel signatures revealed the presence of mismatch-repair deficiency (MMRd) and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) phenotypes, even in cases without germline predisposition. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive characterization of InDel mutagenesis in MM, revealing previously underexplored relationships and demonstrating potential to refine comprehensive genomic classifications of MM.

items.title: High prevalence and diversity of nematodes associated with Europe's most destructive forest pest, revealed by off-target genomic data
items.abstract: We know very little about the biotic interactions of most species on our planet, including many organisms that play a crucial role in ecosystem networks. One highly cost-effective way of reconstructing these networks is to analyse the rapidly growing collections of high-throughput sequencing datasets. In this study, we examine a large whole-genome resequencing dataset for the spruce bark beetle (Ips typographus), one of Europe's most destructive forest pests, to determine the diversity and distribution of associated organisms that such datasets can reveal. We found that from among metagenomic datasets for 312 adult beetles from across the species' European range, 69% contained small subunit ribosomal RNA (SSU rRNA) reads from other eukaryotic organisms, most often nematodes. Among 13 rRNA-reconstructed nematode species, Contortylenchus sp. and Micoletzkya sp. were the most prevalent taxa across the European populations. Frequently, nematode DNA comprised a large proportion of the sequencing libraries, suggesting a significant impact on the host. Mitochondrial genes reconstructed for many of these beetles provided additional phylogenetic resolution, although the reconstruction success varied. Overall, our results demonstrate potential for reconstructing the key biological associations using sequencing data originally generated for a different purpose, highlighting a path towards comprehensive survey of interactions likely to substantially influence the population dynamics of ecologically significant species.

items.title: Distinctive fragmentation of circulating DNA from chromosome Y and its alteration in cancer
items.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cirDNA) fragmentation reflects chromatin organization and represents a promising source of cancer biomarkers. Here, we characterized the fragmentation patterns and nucleosome occupancy of Y chromosome (chrY) cirDNA in healthy individuals and cancer patients. In healthy males, we found that the shorter chrY-derived cirDNA fragments predominantly originate from heterochromatic regions. We also observed substantially lower nucleosome occupancy on chrY than on all other chromosomes, a finding independently supported by micrococcal nuclease digestion data. Remarkably, in patients with colorectal, pancreatic, lung and prostate cancer, the chrY-specific enrichment of shorter fragments was markedly attenuated, contrasting with the increased fragmentation usually observed in cancer when chromosome specificity is disregarded. We reproduced these observations in an independent local cohort of healthy and colorectal cancer patients. We could exploit ratios of short (100-147 bp) to long (147-200 bp) fragments between chrY and other chromosomes to discriminate healthy males from patients with colorectal, pancreatic, and lung cancers with AUCs above 0.98. Autosomes 19, 17, and 22 also displayed atypical fragment patterns, different from chrY and associated with gene density. This last observation was confirmed in females.

items.title: Somatic mutation detection from non-malignant liver tissues using cell-free DNA
items.corresponding_institution: Children's Research Institute, Departments of Pediatrics and Internal Medicine, Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center, Center for Regenerative Science and Medicin
items.abstract: Somatic mutations accumulate in the liver during aging, yet their role in chronic liver disease (CLD) remains unclear due to the difficulty of obtaining liver tissue for analysis. Here, we demonstrate that circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) can be used as a minimally invasive tool to detect liver-derived somatic mutations in patients with CLD. Using ultra-deep targeted duplex sequencing, we show that CLD patients have a higher mutation burden in CLD-associated somatic mutation (CASM) genes compared to healthy individuals. Recurrent driver mutations, including CHD4, INSR, and GPAM, were detected in both liver tissue and cfDNA, with distinct mutational patterns linked to disease etiology: INSR mutations were enriched in metabolic-dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease, while GPAM mutations were associated with alcohol-related liver disease. Liver transplantation led to a significant reduction in CASM mutation burden in cfDNA, providing strong evidence for the diseased-liver origin of these mutations. These findings establish cfDNA analysis as a scalable and noninvasive platform for investigating somatic evolution in non-malignant tissues, offering new opportunities for molecular stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and early detection of CLD progression.

items.title: Large-scale analyses of short open reading frames yield few if any novel human genes
items.abstract: Recent efforts to discover new protein-coding genes in the human genome have yielded a large number of short open reading frames supported by limited experimental evidence supporting translational activity in fragmented parts of those sequences. We examined the 19 highest-confidence predictions made by the TransCODE Consortium, and found that three of them were previously known and thus not novel, while the other 16 could be explained by mechanisms that do not require the assertion of a novel human protein. In several cases, the alternative explanations for the other 16 had already been published. We also analyzed the other 118 predictions and found that most of these, too, could be explained without positing the existence of novel proteins. Our findings show that in the search for new human genes, evidence of transcription and translation can almost always be explained by known mechanisms, and that the predictions of the TransCODE Consortium likely do not include any novel genes.

items.title: The 'near T2T' Canton-S assembly is inconsistent with other Canton-S genomes
items.abstract: Canton-S is among the most widely used Drosophila melanogaster strains, underlying substantial community infrastructure, including serving as a wild-type strain for: genetics studies; studying phenotypes, especially in behavioral studies; and complex trait mapping studies among many others. The recent 'near T2T' assembly of Canton-S (LIU et al.) is presented as delivering modern sequencing and assembly quality to the Drosophila community via this important strain. I find that this assembly is inconsistent with three other independently sequenced Canton-S genome assemblies on a magnitude comparable to differences between distinct strains, raising concerns about its genetic identity that the community should consider when choosing whether to adopt it as a resource.

items.title: Full-length transcript architecture reveals RNA fate and regulatory state
items.abstract: Pervasive transcription generates diverse RNAs, including promoter-upstream transcripts (PROMPTs), coding and non-coding transcripts from protein-coding loci, and enhancer RNAs. How their full-length architectures relate to RNA fate remains poorly understood. Using ultra-deep sequencing of polyadenylated and non-polyadenylated capped RNAs from mouse embryonic stem cells, we show that nuclear exosome surveillance of PROMPTs is associated with transcript length and sequence composition. We show that for most protein-coding genes, capped transcripts are dominated by cytosolic 3'[->]5' degradation intermediates or premature transcription termination products rather than full-length mRNAs. The relative abundance of intact mRNAs, cytosolic degradation intermediates and prematurely terminated transcripts varies between genes and is associated with gene architecture, expression level and biological function. Finally, we identify a class of convergently transcribed enhancers enriched for Polycomb repressive complex 2-associated proteins and poised enhancer features, with an increased propensity for activation during differentiation. Full-length transcript architecture thus reveals RNA fate and regulatory state.

items.title: Annotated reference genome for the Critically Endangered, paleoendemic Bermuda skink (Plestiodon longirostris)
items.abstract: Skinks, one of the largest vertebrate families with over 1,500 described species, are represented by only 19 publicly available chromosome-level genome assemblies. Here, we present the first whole-genome assembly of the Bermuda skink, Plestiodon longirostris, a Critically Endangered, evolutionarily distinct, and endemic species. We conducted a de novo genome assembly using Oxford Nanopore Technology long reads, followed by reference-guided scaffolding against the five-lined skink Plestiodon fasciatus and Gilberts skink Plestiodon gilberti genomes. We generated a 1.496 Gb assembly with 2,579 scaffold contigs over 500 bp in length, a scaffold N50 of 224.1 Mb, with 98.7% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) completeness score and 94.8% of gene annotations transferred from the P. fasciatus annotated genome. Repetitive elements comprised 48.37% of the genome, including 33.79% unclassified repeats, while 9% of transposable element sequences contained internal stop codons, consistent with other reptile genomes. Synteny analysis revealed strong conservation of macrochromosomes and gene order through the Plestiodon genus, and progressive chromosomal rearrangement with increased phylogenetic distance across the wider skink family. We also present the first mitogenome for the species. These genomic resources will further evolutionary research in the skink family and will facilitate applied conservation genomic approaches in this Critically Endangered species.

items.title: BioSensor-X: A Coverage-Aware Evidence-Integration and Benchmarking Framework for Transcription-Factor Prioritization in Microbial Biosensor Engineering
items.corresponding_institution: A.V. College of Arts, Science & Commerce (Autonomous), Osmania University
items.abstract: Transcription-factor (TF) prioritization in microbial biosensor engineering requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and regulatory evidence, yet benchmark-associated performance may be influenced by candidate coverage, annotation density, and information-flow structure. BioSensor-X was developed as a leakage-controlled, coverage-aware framework for evaluating heterogeneous transcriptomic and regulatory evidence for Escherichia coli TF prioritization. Six transcriptomic datasets were processed, of which three contributed candidate instances, yielding 360 candidate contexts representing 60 TFs. The framework integrated transcriptional responsiveness, regulatory specificity, regulon size as an annotation-density proxy, and curated regulatory evidence using discovery-only standardization, prespecified equal weighting, and TF-level maximum aggregation. Performance was evaluated using mutually exclusive TF-level DEVELOPMENT and LOCKED TEST partitions with family-aware stratification, while candidate coverage was assessed separately from conditional ranking performance. Of 12 LOCKED TEST TFs, five were represented in the discovery candidate universe, corresponding to 41.7% coverage. The primary BioSensor-X score achieved a conditional AUROC of 0.5782 (95% bootstrap CI, 0.3308-0.8109), with 1/5 TFs recovered in the Top-10 and 2/5 in the Top-20. The regulon-size/annotation-density component achieved an AUROC of 0.7945 (95% bootstrap CI, 0.6655-0.9055). The integrated framework retained a measurable benchmark-associated ranking signal, while the results also indicated that annotation structure contributed substantially to benchmark discrimination. These findings support the value of separating candidate coverage from conditional ranking performance and explicitly accounting for annotation-density-associated effects when evaluating TF prioritization frameworks.

items.title: Benchmarking sample mispairing detection tools in complex cancer datasets
items.corresponding_institution: University of Colorado School of Medicine
items.abstract: Sample mispairs are common and potentially costly mistakes, and therefore checking for sample mispairing is a crucial quality-control step in multimodal genomic studies. This study presents an independent benchmark of sample mispairing detection tools in multimodal transcriptomic cancer datasets. In pseudobulk experiments with known sample pairings, four tools achieved near-perfect F1 scores across datasets. In real-data experiments, three tools performed particularly well, and sample mispairs were identified in three of five datasets. Finally, a high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma dataset is reconstructed: resolving mispairs between two bulk RNA-sequencing modalities, resolving mispairs between pooled single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data, and reestablishing the connection between the transcriptomic data and patient metadata using genetic ancestry inference.

items.title: Biomedical Text Embeddings Weakly Capture Chromatin Accessibility Similarity: A Large-Scale Measurement Study
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Illinois Chicago
items.abstract: Text metadata provides the most readily available description of public chromatin accessibility data, but it remains unclear how well it reflects similarity between the underlying chromatin profiles. We systematically compared pairwise cosine similarity matrices derived from 12 embedding types across 32,245 human assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (ATAC-seq) experiments obtained from ChIP-Atlas. The embeddings were two chromatin representations (Atacformer and regulatory potential, RP), three biomedical language models and one general-domain model applied to full metadata and to cell-type names alone, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), and a random baseline. We measured agreement using Spearman rank correlation, Mantel permutation tests, and top-k neighborhood overlap in the similarity matrices. Across the full dataset, text-derived similarities correlated with Atacformer similarities at {rho}=0.20 to 0.30. This text-Atacformer agreement was largely driven by experiments with relatively few called peaks, which were enriched for promoter regions (median 69 to 75% within 1 kb of a transcription start site for experiments with 100 to 10,000 peaks), resulting in similar chromatin representations regardless of cell type. Among the 17,232 experiments with at least 5,000 peaks, the text-Atacformer correlations dropped substantially ({rho}=0.011 to 0.016), with less than 0.1% of top-5 neighbors shared. Atacformer itself barely tracked cell type in this subset, with only 1.3% of an experiment's top-5 neighbors sharing its cell-type label (0.8% expected by chance). In contrast, text-RP agreement was weak but persisted ({rho}=0.06 to 0.10; 28 to 35% of top-5 neighbors shared), suggesting that both capture coarse cell-type identity. Most of the text-derived similarity signal in the full dataset came from sample titles, which mainly identify the submission and sequencing platform. Notably, TF-IDF matched or exceeded the language models in every correlation comparison. These findings indicate that text metadata is at best a coarse proxy for chromatin accessibility similarity, and highlight the importance of controlling for peak count when comparing chromatin representations across public repositories.

items.title: Fast draft assemblies using locally consistent parsing
items.abstract: Recent improvements in long-read sequencing accuracy, particularly the introduction of PacBio HiFi reads, have created new opportunities for more efficient sequence representations in genome assembly. In particular, variations of de Bruijn graphs (dBG), such as sparse dBG and minimizer-space dBG, provide efficient representations of sequences and have enabled genome assemblers to leverage the high accuracy of long-read data while maintaining low memory usage and fast analysis times. Locally consistent parsing (LCP) is another technique for compact sequence representation that partitions a string into nearly uniform, highly distinctive substrings in a consistent manner. In this work, we combine ideas from minimizer-space assembly and LCP to achieve a significant speedup in HiFi long-read assembly. Specifically, we define a locally consistent de Bruijn Graph (lcDBG), in which string partitions serve as the graph's building blocks. We introduce Gallifrey, a rapid PacBio HiFi assembler that outperforms the fastest existing tool, rust-mdbg, by >6x in runtime while requiring 2x less memory, assembling a human genome in under one minute on a standard laptop, while generating assemblies with comparable contiguity. Code for Gallifrey is freely available at https://github.com/BilkentCompGen/gallifrey.

items.title: In silico pipeline for identification of targets of plastic-derived chemicals
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a growing global health concern, yet the specific human protein targets mediating the toxic effects of plastic-derived chemicals (PDCs) remain largely unknown. Here, we present an integrative in silico pipeline that combines transcriptomic data with structural bioinformatics to identify putative human plastic-derived targets. Through comparative analysis with their canonical ligands, we identified 27 potential targets showing global binding energies comparable to endogenous ligands (-5.26 vs -5.60 kcal/mol), and six cases in which plastic-derived compounds performed better. Chemical similarity analysis revealed very low structural resemblance between PDCs and canonical ligands, indicating that PDCs do not act as structural mimetics but instead exploit different interactions within the same binding cavities. In a proof-of-concept case, we showed that Deoxyribonuclease I (DNase I) binds BP2 with higher affinity than its canonical ligand PO-3 (median -5.85 vs -2.55 kcal/mol). It also forms hydrogen bonds with Asn192 and {pi}-stacking interactions with the catalytic histidine His274, a pattern conserved in bovine DNase I. Experimental validation confirmed that BP2 at 10- M inhibits DNA hydrolysis by 21.5% in bovine DNase I (p-value < 0.01) and 23.2% in recombinant human DNase I (p-value < 0.001). Our work establishes a robust, transferable computational framework for identifying protein targets of environmental contaminants and reveals that PDCs engage their targets through novel non-mimetic binding modes, with structural patterns that can be conserved across species. These findings may have significant implications for the safety assessment of plastic additives.

items.title: APEs: Agentic Prediction of Epitopes to Guide Antibody-Antigen Structure Prediction
items.abstract: Antibody-antigen complex prediction remains difficult because the surface recognized by a specific antibody is often uncertain, and model confidence may not distinguish alternative poses. We developed APEs (Agentic Prediction of Epitopes for Structure Prediction), an agentic system that retrieves public evidence, interprets predicted antibody and antigen structures, and produces ranked residue-level epitope hypotheses. For retrospective evaluation, web retrieval was restricted to sources released before each CASP target entry date. Across eight CASP16 and six released CASP17 targets, the top-ranked patch reached residue precision of at least 0.5 for nine of 14 targets. We then used the predicted epitopes to steer additional Protenix-v1 sampling and to compare steered finalists with the highest ipSAE unsteered model. The retrospective best selection across three independent router calls increased mean DockQ from 0.306 to 0.375; DockQ increased from 0.089 to 0.679 for H2321 and from 0.005 to 0.379 for H2346. These results show that publicly available evidence specific to the target antibody-antigen complex can serve as an inference-time signal for epitope localization, guided complex sampling, and model selection. We also release predictions for CASP17 targets whose experimental structures had not been released when the predictions were finalized, providing a prospective test of APEs (https://github.com/CSSB-SNU/ape).

items.title: Unipept in 2026: A Unified Web Platform for Comparative Metaproteomics Analysis
items.abstract: Metaproteomics studies the collective proteome of microbial communities to characterize their taxonomic composition and functional activity. Unipept has long supported such analyses, but organizing samples into projects, building targeted reference databases, and comparing samples across a study were only possible in a standalone desktop application. Here we present a major update that moves these workflows into the web application, so a complete multi-sample study can be assembled, analyzed, and shared without local installation. Samples can be compared both taxonomically and functionally, the latter by mapping enzymes onto metabolic pathways with the integrated PathwayPilot. The analyses also became more informative. The Peptonizer2000, now accelerated by the new NORI inference engine, adds confidence scores to taxonomic and functional results, and an optional filter removes common contaminants before analysis. The Unipept API itself was also reworked, with an optimized index and flexible memory loading that roughly doubled query throughput and lowered the memory needed for deployment. We demonstrate these capabilities on six datasets of a defined microbial community.

items.title: The neural basis of unfamiliar face recognition in humans with fMRI frequency-tagging
items.corresponding_institution: Centre de Recherche Cerveau et Cognition, Universite Toulouse 3 Paul Sabatier, CNRS, 31052 Toulouse, France
items.abstract: Faces provide the most diagnostic information for identifying individuals in humans. Understanding the neural mechanisms involved in face identity recognition (FIR) is particularly important for unfamiliar faces, for which identity cannot rely on encoded multimodal semantic associations. Here, we investigated the neural basis of FIR using an original frequency-tagging fMRI approach providing objective, sensitive, and reliable measures of face recognition. Ten human participants were presented within a rapid 6 Hz stream of natural images of a single unfamiliar identity in two conditions: (1) with the same face image across low-level changes (size, luminance, contrast) only, or (2) with images varying in background, size, head orientation, gaze direction, etc. Every 9 s during a 243 s run, seven images of different unfamiliar identities were introduced in bursts. For each participant and each condition, we recorded runs with upright and inverted faces. Analyses were performed within face-selective regions (defined from a frequency-tagging localizer) and in the Fourier domain, where individual face discrimination responses were objectively identified and quantified at the identity-change frequency (0.111 Hz). We observed robust image-based individual face discrimination responses across both conditions in core face-selective ventral regions (LatMidFG and IOG). In contrast, responses in early visual cortex and the pSTS were negligible in our second condition, which required generalization across viewpoint variations. In addition, the LatMidFG showed a reliable inversion effect, confirming that the observed responses cannot be attributed solely to low-level image differences. Overall, these findings highlight the value of fMRI frequency-tagging for objectively characterizing the cortical network underlying unfamiliar FIR, providing evidence for high-level discrimination and generalization of unfamiliar face identity in the human ventral occipito-temporal face-selective network.

items.title: ELLA-mix: Detecting Cell-to-Cell Heterogeneity in Subcellular RNALocalization
items.abstract: Subcellular RNA localization can differ between cells expressing the same gene, yet most analyses summarize transcript positions with a single gene-level pattern. We propose ELLA-mix, a finite mixture model for identifying cell subpopulations with distinct radial localization patterns from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data. Transcript positions are normalized relative to the cell boundary and modeled using flexible spline densities within a count-conditioned nonhomogeneous Poisson process framework. Conditioning on each cell's transcript count separates differences in localization from differences in abundance. We estimate component densities and cell memberships using an expectation-maximization algorithm and select the number of patterns using the Bayesian information criterion, restricting consideration to models with stable cell assignments and sufficiently distinct components. Simulation studies evaluated the type I error and power of the test for nonuniform localization, as well as the accuracy of selecting the number of mixture components and estimating their radial distributions. ELLA-mix correctly selected the number of components in most simulated settings. In seqFISH+ mouse fibroblasts, ELLA-mix identified distinct cell subpopulations for genes previously assigned a single localization class; genes showing such variation were enriched for endoplasmic reticulum and extracellular matrix functions. In Xenium ovarian cancer tissue, more peripheral localization patterns were associated with higher proportions of proliferating cells, particularly in S phase. These results show how modeling cell-to-cell variation can reveal localization patterns and biological associations obscured by gene-level summaries.

items.title: The Dark Side of Light: Adolescent Light Exposure at Night Disrupts Hippocampal Clocks and Plasticity-Related Signaling in a Sex-Dependent Manner.
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Drug Discovery and Biomedical Sciences, University of South Carolina, Columbia, SC, USA
items.abstract: In today's society, adolescents are being increasingly exposed to artificial blue light at night from electronic devices, raising concerns about its effects on brain development and mental health. The hippocampus, and specifically the dentate gyrus (DG) regulates memory formation and itself operates as a subordinate circadian oscillator detecting changes in the light environment. However, whether light at night during adolescence can impair hippocampal clock and function remains unknown. To begin exploring this, we exposed adolescent mice to a light cycle disruption (LCD) paradigm consisting of 12hrs of light followed by 5hrs of darkness and 7hrs of blue-enriched light for 5 consecutive days per week, followed by a standard 12 hours of light and 12 hours of darkness (12L:12D) for 2 days, over a 4-week period. Control animals were maintained under standard 12L:12D. Female and male mice were then tested for novel object recognition (NOR) and novel object location (NOL), and brain tissues were collected for clock gene expression, neuroplasticity markers, and dendritic spine analyses. We found that male mice exposed to LCD spent less time exploring novel objects and locations, and more time with familiar ones, a pattern consistent with impaired recognition and spatial memory, while female mice showed preserved memory performance despite LCD exposure. LCD-exposed male mice showed altered hippocampal daily expression rhythms of Clock and CRY2 levels compared to male control and LCD-exposed females. In addition, we found that LCD-exposed males exhibited reduced p-CREB expression along with reduced Bdnf and dendrite spines numbers in the DG. Interestingly, returning LCD-exposed males to standard 12L:12D conditions for 4 weeks were sufficient to reverse both the behavioral and molecular phenotypes. Together, these results suggest that chronic exposure to light at night during adolescence impairs memory in male mice, through alteration in hippocampal circadian clock regulation and plasticity-related mechanisms within the DG.

items.title: PTMlink: a database resource for co-variation of glycosylation and phosphorylation in human tumors
items.abstract: Protein glycosylation and phosphorylation can regulate each other, but the two protein modifications are usually studied separately, and their modification-specific co-variation across tumor types remains poorly characterized. PTMlink is a database of site-resolved co-variation between glycosylation and phosphorylation in the matched glycoproteomes and phosphoproteomes of 1,211 tumor samples from cohorts of the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium, complemented by studies that perturbed glycosylation in human cells to examine its crosstalk with, and functional effects on, phosphorylation. Eligible glycosite- phosphosite pairs are scored within each tumor cohort by a covariate-adjusted partial rank correlation and combined across cohorts by meta-analysis, where specific glycoforms are scored in the same way and gene pairs are summarized. The strongest associations reproduce in held-out tumor types and show concordance in normal adjacent tissue, and the strongest pairs are enriched for known protein interactions and shared pathways; perturbation evidence recovers literature-documented relations that co-variation misses. Available through a website, an R package and a Model Context Protocol server, PTMlink is, to our knowledge, the first resource to provide a queryable score for site-specific relations between glycosylation and phosphorylation across tumor cohorts, with a framework that can extend to other protein modifications as matched measurements become available.

items.title: From hands to tools: evidence for evolutionary precursors of tool processing in macaque cortex.
items.corresponding_institution: Laboratory for Neuro- and Psychophysiology, Department of Neurosciences, KU Leuven Medical School, Leuven 3000, Belgium
items.abstract: In humans, hands are animate effectors and tools are visually dissimilar inanimate objects, yet the brain represents them in closely related cortical systems. Whether this coupling depends uniquely on human tool knowledge or reflects a conserved property of primate cortex is unknown. Using whole brain fMRI (0.22 cubic mm voxels) in macaques viewing images of hands, tools, and other objects, we found that inferotemporal cortex largely followed the animate/inanimate division, with only a few small hand-tool preferring sites. In contrast, parietal and prefrontal areas showed hand-tool representational similarities that were best matched by a neural-network model trained on fine-grained human hand-object interactions rather than by networks optimized for static object recognition or general action recognition. Volumetric functional ultrasound imaging (0.0023 cubic mm voxels) independently showed that tool responses were spatially aligned with human hand, but not monkey hand, responses in posterior parietal cortex. Macaque cortex thus represents tools in relation to the hand even without habitual tool use, consistent with an evolutionarily conserved action related scaffold that may be shaped by longterm visual exposure to human hand tool interactions.

items.title: FiberBrowser: a unified framework for single-molecule genomics
items.corresponding_institution: Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics, Princeton University
items.abstract: Single-molecule footprinting methods are rapidly transforming chromatin biology. They resolve nucleosome positioning, regulatory-factor occupancy, and accessibility on individual DNA fibers, revealing combinatorial heterogeneity that bulk measurements average away. Emerging footprinting methods leverage diverse enzyme systems and sequencing platforms, necessitating tools that can accommodate these systems. We present FiberBrowser, a unified platform that converts these diverse datasets into a common per-molecule representation of nucleosomes, accessible DNA, and subnucleosomal footprints for interactive and scripted analyses. Its inference engine, FiberHMM, weighs each observation against the assay's informative sites and sequence-specific modification probabilities, separating missing information from protection in four assays. FiberBrowser clusters, sorts and compares these calls across thousands of molecules in seconds, linking chromatin architecture to haplotype, CpG methylation and non-reference structural variants on the same molecules. Because the representation is independent of chemistry, models also transfer between assays. A classifier trained on Fiber-seq footprints identifies 12 scDAF-seq cells as lymphoblastoid without retraining, whereas models trained on raw modification patterns fail to transfer. FiberBrowser thus provides a unified, expandable analytical framework for single-molecule chromatin footprinting.

items.title: ModFormer: A unified structure-aware model of transcriptome-wide A-to-I RNA editing
items.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing can recode transcripts without permanently altering the genome. ADAR-catalyzed editing depends on both local sequence and RNA secondary structure, making it difficult to anticipate which sites will be edited or how mutations will change their activity. Moving from observing endogenous A-to-I editing to using it as a programmable molecular tool requires predicting how editing responds to sequence changes. Here, we present ModFormer, a model that integrates RNA sequence representations with predicted secondary structure to predict ADAR-mediated editing. Trained on human data, ModFormer predicts editing sites and rates across substrates and species unseen during training, recovers established sequence and pairing preferences, and anticipates experimentally measured responses to RNA mutations. These predictions prioritize responsive sites in mutational screens and guide an autonomous AI agent toward candidate RNA designs. ModFormer provides a framework for predicting how sequence changes reshape RNA editing and can be adapted to new substrates with limited experimental data.

items.title: One algorithm, tenfold range: measurement non-equivalence makes cross-national dementia prevalence unidentifiable
items.abstract: Background. Cross-national estimates of dementia prevalence rest on brief cognitive batteries scored against fixed cut-offs. Neither whether they measure the same construct everywhere nor how much of any cross-national difference is measurement has been formally quantified. Methods. In 66,890 adults aged [≥]65 from four population-based cohorts (USA 2016, England 2021-2023, 19 European countries 2021, China 2018) we applied a single harmonised algorithm (Langa-Weir, 27 points) and quantified how far the resulting prevalence moved across 1,152 specifications, measurement-invariance and equating models, latent class analysis, bias correction against a US gold standard, mortality and burden-of-disease anchoring, and multiple imputation. Results. Weighted prevalence ranged from 1.25% (95% CI 0.82-1.83) in England to 12.79% (11.69-13.96) in China (10.2-fold; China minus USA 7.43 points, 6.22-8.65), but the median across specifications was 2.3-fold (IQR 1.5-4.4), the 10.2-fold value sitting at the 94.6th percentile. Scalar invariance was rejected ({Delta}CFI -0.066 vs metric), driven by serial-7 subtraction (odds ratios 2.9-3.4). No operating characteristics can reproduce both the US gold standard (10.0%) and the Chinese national estimate (6.0%): the identity implies Se+Sp-1 = -1.86, outside the admissible range, which would require Chinese prevalence of at least 23.9%. A published harmonised-protocol algorithm applied to the English HCAP subsample gave 7.1% (5.7-8.7), 5.7 times the brief-algorithm value in the same population; harmonised-protocol estimates span 1.4-fold rather than 4.3-fold. Conclusions. Absolute cross-national dementia prevalence is not identifiable from brief screening algorithms. Rank order is more stable than level but is itself specification-dependent (China highest in 45%, England lowest in 65%), whereas the relative risk attached to the label is similar across cohorts (pooled mortality hazard ratio 2.14, I{superscript 2} = 0). We propose a seven-item minimum reporting standard, three items of which can be adopted immediately, and show that metric choice moves the global case count tenfold.

items.title: Generalizable mapping of the Epileptogenic Zone from interictal Intracranial EEG using an implant topology-aware Transformer
items.corresponding_institution: Brno Epilepsy Center, First Department of Neurology, St. Anne's University Hospital and Faculty of Medicine, Masaryk University, Member of ERN EpiCARE, Brno, Cz
items.abstract: Presurgical localization of the epileptogenic zone remains a central challenge in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. At the same time, the abundant interictal intracranial EEG (iEEG) data routinely acquired during presurgical evaluation remain an underexploited source of localizing information. We developed an iEEG implant topology-aware transformer that combines interictal iEEG features with electrode coordinates to predict resection targets. The model was trained exclusively on three public datasets (n = 476) and tested on cohorts from five independent centers across three countries (n = 216). In patients with favorable surgical outcomes (Engel I; n = 120), the median area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.71, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.92, outperforming interictal spike rate and clinically defined seizure-onset zone baselines in patients with favorable outcomes (P < 0.05 for both AUPRC and AUROC). Patients with unfavorable outcomes (Engel II-IV; n = 96) had lower prediction-resection alignment (median AUPRC, 0.42), and their highest confidence predictions were located farther from resected tissue (P = 0.005). These findings establish a generalizable framework that integrates neural activity and brain topology to identify epileptogenic tissue from interictal recordings, potentially improving surgical success rates and reducing reliance on resource-intensive seizure capture.

items.title: Disease-specific versus symptom-specific neuroimaging phenotypes across Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, and Small Vessel Disease
