items.corresponding_institution: Oxford Centre for Integrative Neuroimaging (OxCIN), FMRIB, Nuffield Department of Clinical Neurosciences, University of Oxford
items.abstract: Background: Neurodegenerative disorders are common in ageing populations, and arise from several distinct pathophysiological causes. Yet, they also share many symptoms, including cognitive and neuropsychiatric ones. It is unclear to what extent the impact of neurodegeneration on brain systems is unique or shared across disorders, and whether shared symptoms are driven by degeneration of the same brain systems. Methods: We collected data from n=251 participants with Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, Small Vessel Disease, and age-matched healthy controls. All participants underwent harmonized cognitive and neuropsychiatric assessment and were scanned using the UK-Biobank MRI protocol capturing features including brain volume, white matter lesions and microstructure, tract volume, iron content, and functional connectivity. Results: We replicated established case-control brain changes in Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease and Small Vessel Disease compared to healthy controls. Leveraging this joint standardised dataset, we identified distinct neuroimaging features of individual neurodegenerative disorders, providing evidence for robust diagnosis-specific brain changes. Importantly, however, there was also a large degree of transdiagnostic similarity across neuroimaging markers. Testing for transdiagnostic associations between symptoms and brain phenotypes, we found that lower medial frontal pole connectivity to primary motor cortex was preferentially associated with apathy, fatigue, and depression; whereas cingulum microstructure was associated with cognitive deficits across diagnoses. Conclusions: These results demonstrate that different neurodegenerative diseases are characterised by dissociable brain changes, but also common transdiagnostic and symptom-associated features. This suggests that shared symptoms across neurodegeneration may in part be driven by overlapping impact on key brain systems, such as changes in medial frontal pole connectivity and cingulum microstructure. Our work highlights that multimodal imaging biomarkers can help understand and parse symptomatic heterogeneity in neurodegenerative and ageing populations.

items.title: Plasma proteomic markers of cognitive and brain aging in a multi-ethnic cohort
items.corresponding_institution: Hurvitz Brain Sciences Program, Sunnybrook Research Institute, Toronto, Ontario, Canada; Rehabilitation Sciences Institute, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, Univers
items.abstract: Advances in ultrasensitive proteomics offer opportunities to characterize molecular pathways underlying brain aging. We measured 220 plasma proteins using NULISAseq Neuro220 in 250 Chinese, South Asian, and non-Hispanic White older adults (mean age=68.2 years, 70.4% female). Proteins implicated in neurodegenerative diseases (including brain-derived phosphorylated Tau, BDpTau), synaptic function, oxidative stress, and inflammation were associated with poorer cognition. Phosphorylated Tau205 was associated with reduced entorhinal thickness, whereas inflammatory proteins were associated with imaging markers of cerebral small vessel disease. Several findings were replicated in 1,381 participants in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, including associations of BDpTau species, NPTX2, BACE1, TREM1, CCL17, PRDX6, and IGF1R with cognitive decline and clinical progression. Cardiometabolic risk factors were associated with widespread proteomic alterations, many of which were also linked to poorer brain health. These results identify promising molecular markers of brain aging and extend proteomic research to ethnically diverse populations historically underrepresented in Alzheimer's disease research.

items.title: Focal surgical lesions reveal a subthalamic substrate for human wakefulness
items.abstract: How focal subthalamic injury disrupts a distributed arousal system remains incompletely understood. We investigated transient somnolence after unilateral pallidothalamic tractotomy without sedation in 56 patients, including 14 with somnolence. Volume-adjusted probabilistic lesion mapping identified a hotspot dorsal to the lateral hypothalamus (MNI -6.0, -10.5, -4.0 mm; family-wise error-corrected P = 0.011). A model combining peak involvement and log-transformed lesion volume achieved a leave-one-out cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.799. Applied without refitting to two external cohorts comprising 19 patients, it achieved an AUC of 0.830 (95% confidence interval 0.636-0.977; two-sided cohort-stratified exact permutation P = 0.0166). In a supplementary analysis, somnolence-associated lesions had greater map-weighted burden within a published structural connectivity map of consciousness recovery after deep brain stimulation (P = 0.0299). These findings identify a focal subthalamic vulnerability in maintaining human wakefulness, with a lesion-based model discriminating transient somnolence in independent surgical patients.

items.title: At-home ankle and wrist accelerometry and machine learning capture motor impairment and disease progression in ataxia-telangiectasia
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, MA, USA
items.abstract: Background: Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T) is a rare, childhood-onset neurodegenerative disorder for which sensitive, age-appropriate motor outcome measures are needed to support emerging clinical trials. Clinician-rated ataxia scales are limited by subjectivity, low granularity, and floor and ceiling effects. We evaluated whether at-home wearable accelerometry, combined with machine-learned composite scores derived from submovement features, captures cross-sectional motor impairment and longitudinal disease progression in A-T. Methods: 43 children with classic A-T (median age 9.0 years; IQR 5.7-13.4) and 50 age- and sex-matched controls wore GENEActiv accelerometers on the ankle and wrist during one week of natural behavior at home, repeated at 6- to 12-month intervals. From 85 submovement, activity-intensity, and spectral features per sensor site, we trained composite severity models targeting the Brief Ataxia Rating Scale (BARS) gait subscore (ankle) and BARS total score (wrist). Findings: Ankle composite scores correlated strongly with BARS gait (r = 0.88), BARS total (r = 0.88), and caregiver-reported CPCHILD (r = -0.69); wrist composite scores correlated with BARS total (r = 0.88), BARS arm (r = 0.84), and CPCHILD (r = -0.78). Both models discriminated A-T from controls with large effect sizes (ankle Cohen's d = 2.28; wrist d = 2.98) and demonstrated excellent within-week reliability (ICC = 0.95 ankle; 0.92 wrist). The ankle composite captured disease progression sensitively (Mean-to-Standard Deviation Ratio [MSDR] = 0.98; p < 0.0001). In a matched subset with both sensor and clinical data, ankle composite slopes significantly captured progression (Wilcoxon vs zero, p = 0.0036), whereas BARS total (p = 0.079) and BARS gait (p = 0.30) did not. Interpretation: At-home ankle-based wearable accelerometry provides a sensitive, interpretable, and ecologically valid measure of motor function and disease progression in A-T and may serve as a candidate outcome measure for clinical trials.

items.title: Direct tumour-adipocyte contact / Stroma AReactive Invasion Front Areas (TAC/SARIFA) in advanced oropharyngeal cancer
items.corresponding_institution: University Hospital Augsburg, department of ENT, head and neck surgery
items.abstract: Introduction: Stroma areactive invasion front areas (SARIFA) are a histopathological phenomenon at the tumour invasion front characterised by direct tumour-adipocyte contact (TAC). It can be detected on histological Haematoxylin-Eosin (H&E) stained tumour slides. TAC/SARIFA has emerged as a strong negative prognostic factor in several tumour entities. In this monocentric retrospective study, we aim to elucidate the impact of TAC/SARIFA in oropharyngeal cancer. Materials and methods: 78 cases of pT3 to pT4 oropharyngeal squamous cell cancer from 2005 to 2023 and their corresponding lymph nodes were analysed for the occurrence of TAC/SARIFA. Besides, we compared overall survival rates, recurrence-free survival (RFS) and association with biological and pathological tumour characteristics. Results: In total, overall survival was significantly reduced in TAC/SARIFA-positive tumours (p=0.014). Moreover, TAC/SARIFA positive primary tumours are associated with TAC/SARIFA positive lymph nodes (p<0.001) and extranodal extension (ENE) (p=0.032). Finally, RFS in TAC/SARIFA-positive tumours was reduced, but not significantly (p=0.072). No significant difference was found between p16 positive and p16 negative tumours and prevalence of TAC/SARIFA. Conclusion: TAC/SARIFA is a possible prognostically relevant risk factor in oropharyngeal cancer. When detected in the primary tumour or lymph nodes, it is associated with reduced overall survival rates and tendency towards shorter RFS. TAC/SARIFA-positive lymph nodes almost always show ENE.

items.title: Direct RNA sequencing reveals an m6A downregulated on APOEϵ4 RNA in brain from Alzheimer's disease cases and controls
items.abstract: APOE harbors the strongest common genetic risk factors for late-onset Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet its disease mechanism remains incompletely understood. Two missense SNPs jointly define the APOE alleles, with rs429358 distinguishing {epsilon}4 from {epsilon}3, but whether other APOE features, such as mRNA modifications, contribute to APOE-associated AD risk is unknown. Here, we performed deep long-read direct RNA sequencing on human frontal cortex from six AD cases and six controls to characterize native mRNA modifications transcriptome-wide and across AD-relevant genes. We evaluated differential nucleotide modifications between cases and controls transcriptome-wide, and we then performed two association tests within APOE: (1) associations between mRNA modifications and rs429358 alleles in five {epsilon}3/{epsilon}4 heterozygotes; and (2) pairwise associations between co-occurring mRNA modifications. We identified four modifications associated with rs429358--all within 15 nucleotides of the SNP. Among them was an N6-methyladenosine (m6A) located at chr19:44,908,679 (OR = 0.53; p = 1.4x10-109)--five nucleotides upstream of rs429358--that was 14.5 percentage points lower on {epsilon}4-derived mRNA (27.7%) compared to {epsilon}3 (42.2%). This directional difference was observed within each individual, supporting a consistent allele-associated modification pattern (p = 4.2x10-5). We also identified 344 associations among 73 APOE modifications, suggesting a potentially complex, coordinated network of mRNA biological signals within APOE, alone. Our findings suggest that mRNA modifications may contribute to APOE-associated risk, though validation in large independent cohorts and functional experiments will be necessary to determine the biological consequences of these associations and their potential relevance to AD pathogenesis. Together, our findings highlight the potential of allele-resolved direct RNA sequencing to characterize genetic associations with RNA modifications at a major AD risk locus.

items.title: Hypothesis-Driven Thalamic Stereo-EEG Informs Surgical Therapy for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Outcomes in 117 Consecutive Patients
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurosurgery, Harvard Medical School and Mass General Brigham
items.abstract: Objective Thalamic stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is used to characterize seizure networks and guide neuromodulation, yet its safety and clinical utility are incompletely characterized. We examined how thalamic SEEG informs surgical therapy. Methods We reviewed 117 consecutive patients who underwent thalamic SEEG at Massachusetts General Hospital (2020-2025), in whom the anterior (ANT), centromedian (CM), or pulvinar (PUL) nucleus was sampled to test a seizure network hypothesis. We assessed complications, targeting accuracy, the effect of thalamic ictal timing on laterality determination and neuromodulation target selection, and seizure outcomes. Results Small hemorrhages were seen on postoperative imaging for 0.3% of leads (4/1507); all were asymptomatic and none involved a thalamic lead. Targeting accuracy for ANT, CM, and PUL was 81.0%, 94.2%, and 100%, respectively. Early bilateral thalamic ictal signals identified bilateral seizure networks with 75.6% sensitivity and 78.1% specificity, rising to 92.6% sensitivity when bitemporal onset was excluded. Among 52 patients planned for thalamic or thalamocortical responsive neurostimulation (RNS), the pre-SEEG target was revised in 34.6%, including in patients whose cortical hypothesis was unchanged. Most cortical seizure-onset zones did not map to a single thalamic nucleus. Among patients treated with thalamic or thalamocortical RNS, those with early thalamic ictal signals had better seizure outcomes than those without (standardized mean difference 1.71, 95% CI 0.77-2.65). Mean primary seizure reduction was 75.0 +/- 31.7% after RNS (seizure freedom 40.4%) and 90.9 +/- 20.6% after resection or laser interstitial thermal therapy (61.8%). Significance Thalamic SEEG has a safety profile similar to that of non-thalamic SEEG, provides patient-specific information that informs neuromodulation strategy and target selection, and identifies an early thalamic ictal signal that is associated with better seizure outcomes. These findings support hypothesis-driven thalamic sampling in the evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy.

items.title: Chronic pain and cognitive performance in dementia caregivers: Insights from the STELLA and DETECT-AD studies
items.abstract: Background: Approximately 75% of individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias rely on informal caregivers, yet caregiver health, including chronic pain, remains under-addressed. Chronic pain is highly prevalent, functionally limiting, and linked to cognitive vulnerability, but remains understudied in informal caregivers. This study examined differences in pain and cognitive performance between caregivers and non-caregivers. Objective: To compare chronic pain and cognitive performance between dementia caregivers and non-caregivers and determine whether differences persist independent of age. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of longitudinal data from STELLA and DETECT-AD. Ninety-five participants were followed for 12 months. Weekly online questionnaires assessed pain intensity (0-10 scale) and pain interference (Likert scale), while annual in-person evaluations measured cognition using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Group differences were evaluated using t-tests and multivariate regression adjusting for age. Results: Groups were similar in sex and education but differed in age, pain, and cognition. Caregivers were significatnly younger (71.3 vs 77.3 years; p < 0.0001) and caregivers demonstrated significatnly higher global cognitive performance as measured by the MoCA (mean score 26.8 vs 25.2; p = 0.02). After age adjustment, caregivers reported significantly higher pain intensity (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.00-2.01; p = 0.048). Conclusions: Dementia caregivers exhibit greater pain burden despite younger age, highlighting chronic pain as a critical, underrecognized dimension of caregiver health and identifying an important opportunity to expand existing telehealth caregiver support models.

items.title: Automated Classification of Clinical EEG Reports as Normal or Pathological Using Natural Language Processing: A Multi-Centre Study
items.abstract: We evaluated automated classification of 6,829 de-identified free-text EEG reports from 33 Polish hospitals, independently rated by three experts. Three NLP models - fine-tuned PolBERT, a TF-IDF support vector classifier (SVC), and CatBoost - were assessed across seven binary and three-class tasks. Reference labels were derived from mean expert scores, majority voting or the Dawid-Skene (D-S) model, with different treatments of uncertain cases. Inter-rater agreement was moderate (Krippendorff's = 0.585) and below intrarater agreement (Cohen's {kappa} = 0.731 - 0.769); D-S skill rankings differed from unweighted intra-rater {kappa} rankings. PolBERT led on six of seven tasks (binary accuracy 0.876 - 0.952), although its advantage over CatBoost on three-class tasks was not significant. On Task 2A, all models exceeded all individual experts (0.762 - 0.774 vs 0.689 - 0.726). Binary accuracy held at two isolated hospitals; on Task 2A, SVC fell from 0.762 to 0.616, while PolBERT reached 0.797. Errors clustered in disputed reports (accuracy 0.663 - 0.771 in intermediate strata). Exploratory zero-shot Qwen3.8-27B achieved binary accuracy of 0.829 - 0.929, below supervised models, and agreed with experts similarly to their mutual agreement ({kappa} = 0.53 - 0.61 vs 0.47 - 0.63), but favoured pathological labels. Automated classification of Polish clinical EEG reports is feasible across centres, with performance comparable to individual experts. Model probabilities were well calibrated (ECE [≤] 0.035), supporting threshold-based triage. Accuracy depends on expert disagreement and the method used to construct reference labels; label aggregation should therefore be part of the task definition.

items.title: APOE ϵ4 Effects on Cognitive Decline and Progression to Dementia are Sequentially Mediated through Plasma P-tau217 and Hippocampal Atrophy in an Asian Cohort
items.abstract: Background The APOE {epsilon}4 allele is a major genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD) but underlying pathophysiological mechanisms may vary across populations. In Asian cohorts, the relative contributions of plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau217), neurodegeneration, and cerebrovascular disease to {epsilon}4-associated cognitive decline remain unclear. Objective We investigated biomarker pathways linking APOE {epsilon}4 to cognitive trajectories and incident dementia. Methods APOE genotyping, plasma p-tau217 measurement, and neuroimaging were conducted at baseline in the Singapore Harmonization longitudinal cohort. Participants underwent annual comprehensive neuropsychological assessments for five years. We examined {epsilon}4 group differences in p-tau217, regional subcortical volumes, cortical thickness, and white matter hyperintensities (WMH). Serial mediation analyses examined mediating effects of plasma p-tau217 and neuroimaging markers on {epsilon}4 associations with cognitive decline and dementia risk. Results APOE {epsilon}4 was present in 29.4% of cohort (N=659; age=73.5{+/-}8.0 years; female=56.4%; Chinese ethnicity=83.6%). Carriers had higher p-tau217, reduced entorhinal thickness, and smaller hippocampus, amygdala, accumbens, and putamen volumes, but no WMH differences. Pathways from APOE {epsilon}4 through p-tau217 to hippocampal volume ({beta}=-0.009, 95% CI=-0.015, -0.004, 13.8%) and entorhinal thickness ({beta}=-0.008, 95% CI=-0.014, -0.004, 13%) significantly mediated steeper global and domain-specific cognitive decline. APOE {epsilon}4 was associated with increased dementia risk (HR=2.35, 95% CI=1.37-4.06), partially mediated by p-tau217 and hippocampal volume (9%). Direct {epsilon}4 effects were minimal and WMH did not influence these associations. Conclusions APOE {epsilon}4 contributes to cognitive decline and incident dementia through an AD-specific cascade captured by increased p-tau217 and hippocampal atrophy, providing population-specific insights into APOE {epsilon}4-related pathways in older Asian adults.

items.title: Integrating Plasma Brain-Derived pTau217, White Matter Hyperintensity and Hippocampal Volumes as Optimized Prognostic Markers for Cognitive Decline in an Asian Cohort with High Cerebrovascular Disease Burden
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Combination of plasma and neuroimaging biomarkers associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) and cerebrovascular pathophysiology might provide more accurate prediction of cognitive decline in populations with extensive AD and cerebral small vessel disease copathologies. Here, we aimed to identify an optimized biomarker panel for predicting cognitive decline by evaluating combinations of plasma and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) biomarkers. Methods: We investigated participants without dementia or with mild dementia, recruited from memory clinics and the community in Singapore between August 2010 and August 2020. Plasma biomarkers of brain amyloid (brain-derived [BD]-pTau217, BD-pTau181, BD-pTau231, total-pTau217, total-pTau181, and total-pTau231), astrogliosis (GFAP), and neuroaxonal injury (NfL), with MRI measures of cerebrovascular disease (white matter hyperintensity [WMH] volume) and neurodegeneration (hippocampal volume), and primary outcome of longitudinal Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB; mean [SD] follow-up duration, 51.0 [15.8] months). All plasma and MRI biomarker combinations for predicting CDR-SB slope (annual change in CDR-SB) were evaluated. Results: This study included 523 participants (mean [SD] age, 72.4 [7.9] years; 291 females [55.6%]). The parsimonious model included plasma BD-pTau217, WMH volume, and hippocampal volume (all P [≤] 0.004). Dichotomizing these biomarkers yielded A, V, and N status, respectively, classifying participants as all negative (A-V-N-; n = 128), 1-positive (A+V-N-, A-V+N- or A-V-N+; n = 154), 2-positive (A+V+N-, A+V-N+, A-V+N+;n = 158) or 3-positive (A+V+N+; n = 83). Annual CDR-SB progression increased stepwise with the number of positive biomarkers. Compared with the all negative group ({beta}, 0.016), the 1-positive ({beta}, 0.409), 2-positive ({beta}, 1.16) and 3-positive groups ({beta}, 1.49) showed faster cognitive decline (all P < 0.001). Moreover, the 2-positive and 3-positive groups progressed faster than the 1-positive group (both P < 0.001), and the 3-positive group declined faster than 2-positive group (P = 0.009). Conclusions: Presence of multiple pathophysiological processes was associated with greater cognitive decline, highlighting the utility of a comprehensive multimodal biomarker profile to enhance prognostication.

items.title: Integrated real-world and translational studies nominate CREB binding protein/EP3001 inhibition to overcome androgen receptor pathway modulator resistance in men with prostate cancer
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Medicine, Division of Medical Oncology, Duke University Medical Center, Durham, NC; Duke Cancer Institute Center for Prostate and Urologic Cancers
items.abstract: Androgen pathway modulators (APMs) have significantly improved outcomes for men with metastatic prostate cancer, but the evolution of therapy resistance is nearly universal, and there remains a major clinical need to identify actionable vulnerabilities for therapy-resistant disease. To address this need, we employed regulatory network models that leverage multi-omic data from over 10,000 prostate cancer patients with longitudinal clinical data. Analysis of the architecture of the network models identified EP300 as the top actionable target associated with androgen receptor-mediated therapy resistance. These observations were validated using a novel inhibitor of CBP/EP300, pocenbrodib, which showed preclinical activity in vitro and in vivo. Acetylomics analysis and functional studies pinpointed inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid metabolism as key mechanisms of action for pocenbrodib. Clinical benefit for this agent was demonstrated in a patient with metastatic APM-resistant prostate cancer (NCT04575766), highlighting CBP/EP300 as a key target for further translation.

items.title: Long-read sequencing resolves functional CYP2D6 alleles tagged by a cocaine use disorder associated haplotype
items.abstract: The CYP2D6 locus exhibits extensive allelic diversity and structural complexity, complicating the identification of functional variants underlying genetic associations. We previously identified a four-single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) haplotype (AACG) associated with cocaine use disorder and altered CYP2D6 expression in the brain. To characterize the molecular variation of this haplotype, we performed targeted PacBio long-read sequencing on 19 individuals of European ancestry carrying zero, one, or two copies of AACG. Complementary analyses included human pangenome assemblies, protein structural modeling, splice quantitative trait loci, and SNP-array probe sequences. Long-read sequencing resolved distinct CYP2D6 alleles associated with AACG, including CYP2D6 star 2 and star 4. Four of five individuals lacking AACG carried two canonical reference alleles, whereas nearly all AACG homozygotes carried noncanonical alleles. The star 2 allele contained two missense substitutions (R296C and S486T), while star 4 carried four missense substitutions (P34S, L91M, H94R, and S486T) and a loss-of-function splice-site mutation. Structural comparisons suggested potential substrate-dependent effects on ligand binding, while publicly available transcriptomic data associated AACG variants with altered splice-junction usage across multiple tissues, including brain. Although SNP-array intensity differences initially suggested copy-number variation, long-read sequencing did not support consistent gene dosage differences. Instead, polymorphisms within array probe-binding regions provided a plausible explanation for these signals. These findings demonstrate that a disease-associated SNP haplotype tags functionally distinct CYP2D6 alleles and highlight the importance of haplotype-resolved sequencing for interpreting genetic associations at complex pharmacogenomic loci.

items.title: Eating disorder phenotypes differ in their genetic relationships with impulsivity facets
items.abstract: Background. Eating disorders are clinically heterogeneous and characterized by distinct patterns of control over food intake. Anorexia nervosa (AN) is characterized by excessive dietary restraint, whereas binge-eating (BE) is a transdiagnostic behavior defined by loss of control over eating. Understanding the relationship between eating disorders and impulsivity may provide insights into their underlying mechanisms and identify potential targets for prevention and treatment. Methods. We used genome-wide association study data (N=82,707-1,268,116) and genomic structural equation modeling to examine genetic relationships between eating disorder phenotypes (AN, ANRestrictive, ANBinge-Purging, and BE) and impulsivity facets (five UPPS-P, three BIS-11, and delay discounting). We examined whether these relationships persisted after conditioning on the genetic liability for substance use disorders (SUDs) and body mass index (BMI). Results. AN and its subtypes showed negative genetic correlations with delay discounting, the magnitude of this correlation being stronger for ANRestrictive. ANRestrictive also showed negative genetic correlations with sensation seeking and common impulsivity, whereas ANBinge-Purging showed a positive genetic correlation with urgency-specific impulsivity. In contrast, BE showed positive genetic correlations with both common and urgency-specific impulsivity. Several associations remained significant after controlling for SUDs and BMI, including the negative association between AN with delay discounting, the negative associations with AN and ANRestrictive with sensation seeking, and the positive association between BE and urgency-specific impulsivity. Conclusion. These findings reveal complex patterns of genetic overlap between eating disorder phenotypes and impulsivity dimensions. Understanding these phenotype-specific relationships may help explain clinical heterogeneity and inform the development of more targeted prevention and treatment strategies.

items.title: Anatomical and Etiologic Predictors of Oculopalatal Tremor Phenotypes: A Pooled Patient-Level Analysis
items.corresponding_institution: Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center, University Hospitals, Case Western Reserve University
items.abstract: Oculopalatal tremor (OPT) follows disruption of the cerebello-rubro-olivary network and is frequently associated with hypertrophic inferior-olive degeneration (HOD). HOD does not invariably produce OPT; determinants of oculo-palatal, ocular-only, palatal-only, or non-oscillatory phenotypes remain undefined. We analyzed 501 patients with HOD, of which 424 with classifiable laterality: 52.1% had unilateral and 47.9% bilateral HOD. Lesion location predicted HOD laterality (chi-square=35.65, p=3.4x10^-7; Cramer V=0.31): brainstem/pons lesions produced ipsilateral HOD in 70.0%, whereas cerebellar lesions produced contralateral HOD in 86.4%. Bilateral HOD reflected combined cerebellar/brainstem lesions, and was associated with ocular oscillations (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.31-5.43; p=0.0067) but not convincingly palatal oscillations (OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.91-2.42; p=0.137). Phenotype differed by etiology (p=0.0024): hemorrhagic and vascular-malformation lesions preferentially produced combined OPT, ischemic lesions were enriched among ocular-only presentations, and neoplastic lesions produced the most heterogeneous phenotype and were disproportionately represented among palatal-only cases. Age, sex, and lesion laterality were not associated with phenotype. Four-class prediction was limited (macro AUC 0.555; balanced accuracy 0.301), with little improvement after adding HOD laterality (macro AUC 0.563; balanced accuracy 0.323). Among classifiable OPT waveforms, 96.9% contained a pendular component. Median OPT latency was 6 months (IQR 4.75-24); lesion location, etiology, and HOD laterality did not predict latency. HOD is therefore an important substrate, but lesion anatomy and etiology shape group-level phenotype without enabling reliable individual prediction.

items.title: Nigral volume as a marker for Lewy body copathology in Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract: Background: Lewy body (LB) copathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is associated with earlier symptom onset and faster cognitive decline. Depigmentation of substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) volume is seen in both Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. We examined whether lower antemortem SNc volume was associated with autopsy confirmed LB pathology in patients with AD or mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Methods: Seventy-three participants with a clinical diagnosis of AD or MCI, neuromelanin-sensitive MRI, and subsequent neuropathologic assessment from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative were studied. At autopsy, 33 participants had LB pathology (LB+) and 40 had no LB pathology (LB-). We compared SNc volume between groups using analysis of covariance adjusted for age and sex. Within the LB+ group, we assessed the association between SNc volume and nigral hypopigmentation using Spearman correlation. In a secondary analysis, we tested whether adding SNc volume to a logistic regression mode containing age, sex, and executive function improved model fit for autopsy-defined LB status. Results: LB+ participants had greater nigral hypopigmentation at autopsy and lower antemortem SNc volume than LB- participants. The adjusted mean difference in SNc volume (LB+ minus LB-) was -66 mm3 (95% confidence interval -115.9 to -16.2, P=0.010). Within the LB+ group, lower SNc volume was associated with greater hypopigmentation (Spearman rho;=-0.373, P=0.032). Among 71 participants with complete model data, adding SNc volume improved model fit (likelihood ratio=8.67, P=0.003). The combined model had an in sample area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.770 (95% confidence interval: 0.661-0.879). Conclusion: The correspondence between lower antemortem SNc volume and greater hypopigmentation at autopsy supports the use of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI to characterize nigral involvement in AD or MCI with LB copathology. These findings are based on a single cohort, and the interval of several years between imaging and autopsy limits how closely the pigmentation ratings reflect nigral integrity at imaging.

items.title: Dynamic Macro-Microvascular Coupling During Cerebrovascular Reactivity Revealed by Simultaneous TCD and DCS
items.abstract: Background Transcranial Doppler (TCD) measures flow velocity in large intracranial arteries but provides limited information on microvascular perfusion.Diffuse correlation spectroscopy (DCS) enables continuous, noninvasive assessment of cortical microvascular blood flow. We compared macrovascular and microvascular responses during cerebrovascular reactivity testing. Methods Forty-four healthy adults (28 men; mean age, 27.0{+/-}3.8 years) underwent simultaneous bilateral TCD and DCS during a breath-holding task (1-minute baseline, 30-second breath hold, and 1-minute recovery). Middle cerebral artery flow velocity and cortical microvascular blood flow index were normalized to baseline (rCBFv and rCBFi, respectively). Temporal responses were compared using Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Response amplitude, rise time, and recovery time were also assessed. Results TCD and DCS showed concordant response trajectories during breath holding and recovery. Correlations between normalized temporal responses were strong in both hemispheres (left,r=0.988{+/-}0.009;right, r=0.990{+/-}0.008; both P<0.001). Bland-Altman analysis showed minimal systematic bias and no proportional bias. No significant interhemispheric differences were observed in response amplitude, rise time, or recovery time. DCS-derived rCBFi showed greater response amplitudes and variability than TCD-derived rCBFv (left, 1.80{+/-}0.34 vs 1.63{+/-}0.15; right, 1.72{+/-}0.27 vs 1.63{+/-}0.14). Parameter-level analyses showed strong correlations and minimal bias for response amplitude, rise time, and recovery time. Conclusions TCD and DCS demonstrated strong temporal coupling during cerebrovascular reactivity testing, while DCS detected larger response amplitudes than TCD. These findings suggest that macrovascular velocity and cortical microvascular perfusion provide complementary information about cerebrovascular responses.

items.title: Parkinson's disease-associated LRRK2 armadillo domain variants enhance kinase pathway activity through a Rab-binding site-dependent mechanism
items.corresponding_institution: Medical Research Council Protein Phosphorylation and Ubiquitylation Unit, Faculty of Life Sciences, University of Dundee, UK
items.abstract: Pathogenic variants that increase LRRK2 kinase activity are a common genetic cause of Parkinson's disease. Most pathogenic variants occur within the catalytic ROC-COR GTPase (e.g. R1441C) and kinase (e.g. G2019S) domains, where they activate LRRK2 through distinct mechanisms. The common kinase-domain variant directly enhances the intrinsic catalytic activity of LRRK2, whereas ROC-COR variants shift the equilibrium towards its active conformation. Whether variants in the N-terminal armadillo (ARM) domain, which contains Rab GTPase-binding sites involved in LRRK2 membrane recruitment, activate LRRK2 through a different mechanism remains unclear. Here, we characterise the LRRK2 Madrid haplotype, comprising two ARM variants (L119P/L488P) identified in a multigenerational family with PD. In cellular assays, L488P, but not L119P, increased LRRK2-mediated Rab10 phosphorylation approximately two-fold. Increased LRRK2 pathway activity was likewise observed in primary neutrophils and monocytes from variant carriers, including individuals with and without PD. Multiplexed parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) mass spectrometry in neutrophils further demonstrated coordinated increases in phosphorylation of six endogenous Rab substrates (Rab3, Rab8, Rab10, Rab12, Rab35 and Rab43), demonstrating concordant pathway activation in cellular models and primary human blood cells. Mechanistically, L488P lies adjacent to ARM Rab-binding site 1, and its activating effect was abolished by the site-1-disrupting L403E substitution, whereas activation by the ROC-domain variant R1441C was retained. We further investigated five rare ARM-domain variants identified through GP2 and independent genetic datasets, of which two, F470S and V483G, showed increased LRRK2 pathway activity in a site-1-dependent manner, while the remaining three showed no substantial activation. Together, these findings demonstrate that L488P-mediated pathway activation is recapitulated in human variant carriers and depends on an intact ARM Rab-binding site 1, identifying a mechanism of LRRK2 regulation distinct from that of classical catalytic-core variants.
